items.body:
# [Bug]: LLM stream hangs indefinitely on half-dead pooled connections — retry cycle leaks CLOSE-WAIT sockets and memory

## Summary

A gateway turn can hang for minutes with zero progress when its streaming LLM
request lands on a pooled connection the server has already half-closed.
Instead of failing fast, the attempt waits out the full httpx read timeout,
retries (up to 3 attempts), and each aborted attempt leaks the socket in
`CLOSE-WAIT` plus its buffers. On messaging platforms this manifests as an
endless "typing… / not typing…" loop with no reply, and over hours the socket
leak grows RSS by ~200MB/h. The platform is irrelevant — the bug is in the
shared LLM request layer.

## Environment

- Hermes v0.19.1 (upstream 1789e06e), git install
- nemo-relay 0.6.0, openai SDK 2.24.0, httpx 0.28.1
- Provider: DeepSeek (`deepseek-v4-flash`) — **api.deepseek.com is served via
  CloudFront** (resolves to `d3bbv8sr76az5s.cloudfront.net`, lhr3 edge)
- Platforms: Discord (primary), systemd gateway service

## Symptom

- User sends a message; the bot shows typing, stops, shows typing again…
  indefinitely (adapter's persistent typing task keeps re-sending every ~10s;
  the gaps are Discord's 10s display expiry — it is a hang, not a retry storm
  in the adapter)
- Gateway process: alive, systemd active, cron scheduler still ticks
  (executions.db keeps completing), but `~/.hermes/logs/agent.log` goes silent
  mid-turn (no API call lines, no turn end)
- `ss -tnp`: 2–3 sockets in **CLOSE-WAIT** owned by the gateway, all to the
  LLM endpoint (CloudFront lhr3), while Discord/Cloudflare sockets are healthy

## Observed timeline (2026-07-31, two incidents on the same host)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 04:20 | Turn with heavy tool use; `RuntimeError: scope handle is not at the top of the stack` (#73746); gateway drained, exited 75, systemd restarted. RSS 2.0G peak |
| 13:36 | Same #73746 scope error during background skill-save turn; messaging dead; 1 log line in 49 min; RSS 2.3G (peak 3.1G) |
| 14:26 | Manual restart. Fresh RSS 205MB |
| 15:04:34 | User message → new session → skill loads → voice transcription (faster-whisper) completes 15:05:05 |
| 15:05:05+ | **Turn silent.** No `API call #2`, no turn end. 3× CLOSE-WAIT sockets appear on the CloudFront/DeepSeek endpoint |
| 15:09:30 | Manual restart (typing loop ongoing ~4 min). Would likely have self-resolved at ~15:11 via the kimi-k3 fallback leg after 3×120s retries |

The 3 CLOSE-WAIT sockets correspond to 3 stream attempts: each aborted attempt
abandons its socket without closing it.

## Root-cause analysis (from code)

- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py::_call_chat_completions` (streaming path):
  - httpx read timeout: `HERMES_STREAM_READ_TIMEOUT` default **120s**
    (`env_float`, line ~2981)
  - `HERMES_STREAM_RETRIES` default **2** → 3 total attempts (line ~3682)
  - SDK retries disabled (`max_retries=0`) — outer loop owns retries (good)
  - `_stream_stale_timeout` is `None` for cloud providers, so the
    stale-stream detector never arms for the generic path; only the Codex
    path gets the no-byte TTFB watchdog (`_codex_watchdog_enabled =
    agent.api_mode == "codex_responses"`)
- CloudFront closes idle keep-alive connections; the httpx pool keeps the
  half-closed socket (FIN received → CLOSE-WAIT, never reaped)
- A request on that socket gets zero bytes; httpx read timeout (120s) fires;
  retry; repeat → up to ~6 min silent, then fallback chain or error
- **Abandoned attempts leak the socket + buffers** (CLOSE-WAIT pile-up,
  ~200MB/h RSS growth under sustained use) — the same leak likely drove the
  2.0–2.3G RSS at both earlier incidents

## Why it's not platform-specific

The streaming + retry machinery is in the shared agent layer; `gateway.run`
handles all platforms identically. Discord/Telegram/WhatsApp would all show
the same hang. Platform-specific symptoms are cosmetic: Discord's typing loop,
and `50006: Cannot send an empty message` when the final (post-stream) send
carries empty content after a streamed delivery.

## Expected behavior

1. A half-dead pooled connection should be detected and closed at reuse
   (pool should reap CLOSE-WAIT sockets), failing the attempt in seconds, not
   the full read timeout
2. The no-byte TTFB / stale watchdog should apply to the generic streaming
   path, not just Codex
3. Cancelled/superseded stream attempts must close their sockets (no
   CLOSE-WAIT accumulation, no buffer leak)

## Workarounds (current)

- Restart the gateway (`hermes gateway restart`) to clear stuck turns and
  leaked sockets
- `HERMES_STREAM_READ_TIMEOUT=60` (systemd drop-in on the unit) shrinks the
  silent window per attempt from 120s → 60s, so the fallback chain engages in
  ~3 min instead of ~6
- External watchdog: restart when the gateway holds ≥2 CLOSE-WAIT sockets
  (healthy gateway has 0) — deployed as a 5-min cron on this host

## Related

- #73746 — relay scope-stack corruption: same host, same symptom class
  (silent messaging, alive gateway), possibly same cancellation-path root
  (abandoned stream attempts without proper cleanup)
- #58962 — cross-turn stale-call circuit breaker (Codex path only)

items.title: Desktop sidebar session pin/unpin does not persist: backend PATCH rejects 'pinned' (400, error swallowed)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary
In the Hermes desktop app, pinning/unpinning a session in the sidebar only works for the current UI session. The pin is written to localStorage, but the backend never persists it: the desktop sends `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` with `{"pinned": true/false}`, and the API server rejects it with HTTP 400.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open Hermes desktop, click the pin icon on a session in the sidebar. It appears pinned (localStorage).
2. Restart the desktop app (or clear localStorage / reinstall). The pin is gone.
3. Any backend-side operation that considers session state (e.g. auto-archive) does not know the session is pinned.

## Root cause
`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`, `_handle_patch_session` only accepts `{"title", "end_reason"}`:
```python
allowed = {"title", "end_reason"}
unknown = sorted(set(body) - allowed)
if unknown:
    return self._error_response(request, 400, "Unsupported session fields: ...")
```
The desktop side (`apps/desktop/src/store/session-pin-sync.ts`) sends `pinned` and swallows the resulting 400 with `.catch(() => {})`, so the failure is silent.

Additionally, `_session_response` safe_keys does not include `pinned`/`archived`, so GET /api/sessions never reports the persisted value.

`SessionDB.set_session_pinned` exists (`hermes_state.py`) with roundtrip tests, but no HTTP endpoint calls it.

## Environment
- Hermes v0.19.1 (2026.7.30), installed from git
- Confirmed present on upstream `main` @ `126ff7071` (same `allowed = {"title", "end_reason"}` line)

## Suggested fix
1. `_handle_patch_session`: accept `pinned` (bool) and `archived` (bool, same class of bug) and call `db.set_session_pinned` / `db.set_session_archived`.
2. `_session_response`: include `pinned`/`archived` in the serialized session so clients can reconcile.
3. (Optional) advertise these fields in `/v1/capabilities` so clients know the backend supports them.

labels.name: comp/cli

labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
xAI OAuth token exchange succeeds intermittently, but credential does not persist in Hermes auth store

Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.17.0
- Python: 3.13.5
- Runtime: Docker container on VPS
- Project path: /opt/hermes
- Provider configured in hermes status: xAI Grok OAuth (SuperGrok / Premium+)

Problem

I’m trying to use xAI Grok OAuth in Hermes, but the OAuth flow appears unstable and the credential does not persist in the auth store.

After repeated attempts:

- hermes auth list does not show xai-oauth
- hermes status --all shows xAI OAuth: not logged in
- Hermes still reports Provider: xAI Grok OAuth

Reproduction steps

Run:
hermes auth add xai-oauth --type oauth --manual-paste --no-browser --timeout 120
Hermes prints an authorize URL like:
https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A56121%2Fcallback&scope=openid+profile+email+offline_access+grok-cli%3Aaccess+api%3Aaccess&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256&state=...&nonce=...&plan=generic&referrer=hermes-agent
Then:

1. Open the authorize URL in a browser
2. Sign in to xAI
3. Approve access
4. Paste the returned callback/code into the same terminal session

Observed errors

I’ve seen the following errors across repeated attempts:

- xAI authorization failed: state mismatch
- xAI token exchange failed (HTTP 400): {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"PKCE verification failed"}
- xAI token exchange failed (HTTP 400): {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"Invalid or unknown authorization code"}

On one attempt Hermes printed:
Saved xai-oauth OAuth credentials: "loopback_pkce"
But after that, the credential still did not show up in the auth list or status output.

Expected behavior

After a successful xAI OAuth login:

- hermes auth list should show xai-oauth
- hermes status --all should report xAI OAuth as logged in
- the auth store should contain the xAI credential Hermes is using

Actual behavior

- OAuth flow intermittently fails with state mismatch or PKCE/code exchange errors
- A save message appears once, but the credential does not persist in the auth store Hermes uses
- Hermes still reports xAI OAuth as not logged in

Files / checks I used

- /opt/data/auth.json
- hermes auth list
- hermes status --all

Questions

1. Is there a recommended reset / cleanup procedure for xAI OAuth in Hermes?
2. How can I verify which auth store / profile the gateway is using?
3. Is there a known issue with xAI OAuth persistence or PKCE in v0.17.0?
4. Is there a supported way to fully recreate the xAI auth state from scratch?

Notes

I’m using my Grok subscription via OAuth — not an API key.

---

items.title: Windows: hermes update always fails with "Hermes is still running" while Desktop backend locks venv .pyd files

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Bug Description

`hermes update` (and the in-app update button) always fails on Windows with:

```
✗ Another Hermes update is already running (PID XXXX, started Xs ago).
error=Some("Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again.")
```

even after closing all Hermes windows. The update never proceeds while the Hermes Desktop app is running.

## Root Cause (confirmed via logs)

The Hermes Desktop backend process locks the venv's native extension files on Windows:

1. Hermes Desktop starts → spawns `venv\python.exe -m hermes_cli.main serve` (in older versions: `python -m maya_mcp.server`) as its backend
2. Python loads `.pyd` native extensions from the venv → Windows memory-maps those files → **file locks**
3. `hermes update` needs to replace those dependency files → blocked by the locks
4. When triggered from inside the desktop UI, the desktop process never exits (it cannot kill itself), so the updater detects "Hermes is still running" forever
5. Retrying spawns another updater process, which detects the previous one → "Another Hermes update is already running" self-detection deadlock

Hermes's own update log confirms it (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\logs\hermes-update.log`):

```
✗ Other Hermes processes are running from this install's venv:
  PID 88760  python.exe  python -m maya_mcp.server  ← Hermes Desktop backend (close the desktop app)

  On Windows these keep native extension files (.pyd) locked, so the
  dependency update would fail partway and leave a broken install.
  Close the Hermes desktop app / other Hermes terminals, then re-run:
    hermes update
  (or use `hermes update --force-venv` to proceed anyway at your own risk)
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Hermes Desktop on Windows
2. Click the update button in the UI (or run `hermes update` from a terminal while the desktop is open)
3. Observe the failure: "Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again."
4. Close all Hermes windows — the error persists with "Another Hermes update is already running"

## Expected Behavior

- The in-app update button should gracefully shut down the desktop backend first (or the updater should kill its own parent process tree / the venv python backend before attempting the dependency update)
- The updater's "another update already running" check should not flag its own just-spawned child
- On Windows, the updater should handle .pyd memory-mapped locks: e.g., before replacing venv files, terminate processes whose executable path is inside the install's venv (similar to what `hermes update` already does for the gateway, but extended to the desktop backend), or defer the dependency swap until the next launch

## Actual Behavior

The update fails every time while the desktop is running. The only workaround is a fully manual sequence from an external terminal: kill all `Hermes.exe`, kill all `python.exe` whose `ExecutablePath` is inside `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\...\venv\`, kill `node.exe`, then run `hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main`, then relaunch the desktop.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10 (10.0.19045)
- Hermes version: 0.19.1 (also affected 0.17.0)
- Install: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\` (bootstrap install)
- Desktop app + venv backend (`hermes_cli.main serve`)

## Suggested Fix (for maintainers)

In the updater on Windows, before the dependency update stage:

1. Enumerate `python.exe` processes and match `ExecutablePath` against the install venv (`<hermes_home>/hermes-agent/venv/`)
2. Terminate those processes (they are the desktop backend / gateway)
3. Optionally verify no `.pyd` file is still mapped before proceeding

This mirrors what the log message already tells users to do manually — the updater could just do it itself. Also worth fixing: the "another update already running" check should ignore processes that are children of the same parent that triggered the update.

items.title: [Bug] Windows: hindsight embedded daemon pops black console windows (uv venv pythonw.exe is a console-subsystem trampoline)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

labels.name: area/memory
labels.description: Memory subsystem: store, providers, sync, background reviews

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, the Hindsight **local_embedded** daemon pops a black console window every time it starts. Because the daemon idles out after 300s and is restarted on demand, the flash repeats periodically while using Hermes.

## Environment

- Windows 10/11
- Hermes install created with **uv 0.12** (`uv venv`) — `venv/pyvenv.cfg` shows `uv = 0.12.0`
- `hindsight-embed 0.8.6`, mode `local_embedded`

## Root cause

1. `DaemonEmbedManager._find_api_command()` → `_windows_gui_interpreter(scripts_dir)` picks `venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe` — the intent (per the docstring, issue #1885) is to use the GUI-subsystem interpreter so no console is allocated.
2. **But uv 0.12-created venvs ship `venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe` as a CONSOLE-subsystem trampoline** — `file` reports `PE32+ executable ... (console)`, and it forwards to the base interpreter's `python.exe` (console), not `pythonw.exe`.
3. A console-subsystem process with no attached console **allocates a new console window** on start. `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` (used in `_detach_popen_kwargs`) does not help because the trampoline's own CreateProcess call decides the child's subsystem/console behavior.

Process chain observed:

```
pythonw.exe (venv\Scripts, console-subsystem trampoline)
  └─ python.exe (base interpreter, %APPDATA%\uv\python\cpython-3.11-...\python.exe)
       -m hindsight_api.main --daemon --idle-timeout 300 --port 9177
```

## Reproduction

```
file venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe        :: PE32+ executable ... (console)  ← not GUI
venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe -c "import time; time.sleep(3)"   :: console window appears
```

## Suggested fix (verified locally)

In `_windows_gui_interpreter()`, prefer the **base interpreter's real GUI-subsystem `pythonw.exe`** (`sys._base_executable` sibling — e.g. `%APPDATA%\uv\python\cpython-3.11-...\pythonw.exe`) over the venv shim, and point `PYTHONPATH` at the venv's `site-packages` so `-m hindsight_api.main` still imports:

```python
base = getattr(sys, "_base_executable", None) or sys.executable
try:
    base_pythonw = Path(base).with_name("pythonw.exe")
    if base_pythonw.exists():
        return str(base_pythonw)   # GUI subsystem — never allocates a console
except OSError:
    pass
# ... existing venv-shim fallback
```

plus, in the daemon env builder:

```python
env["PYTHONPATH"] = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)  # venv site-packages
```

Verified: after this change the daemon starts with **no console window** (a GUI-subsystem process never allocates a console regardless of creation flags). User-confirmed in production.

## Why this matters beyond cosmetics

The console trampoline also **maps `venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe` while running**, which breaks in-place updates (Windows mandatory file locks → the updater hits Access Denied while syncing the venv and strands it half-updated). A proper fix here removes one of the lock-holder classes the update path has to work around — see PR #75477 for the desktop-side generic mitigation.

items.title: [Bug]: Security audit OSV client fires 13 DNS queries/second — 779K queries in 16 hours

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

When an MCP server fails to start (e.g. `time` and `fetch` servers), the Hermes gateway's `mcp_stdio_watchdog.py` enters an aggressive revival loop. Each revival attempt calls `uvx mcp-server-<name>`, which:

1. Downloads the Python package from **pypi.org** (new connection per attempt)
2. Triggers `check_package_for_malware()` which queries **api.osv.dev** for vulnerability data

This generates massive DNS/network traffic: **779,427 queries to api.osv.dev + 72,000 queries to pypi.org** in a 16-hour window.

## Evidence

### Pi-hole DNS Log Analysis
- **api.osv.dev**: 779,427 queries in 16h (Jul 30) — ~13 queries/second, 24/7
- **pypi.org**: 72,000 queries in same period — from `uvx` package downloads
- All queries from Hermes host, pattern: `A → AAAA → A → AAAA` at 1-second intervals

### Process Analysis (host .86)
```
PID 425353: hermes gateway run (since Jul 29)
   └── 91× mcp_stdio_watchdog.py -- /root/.local/bin/uvx mcp-server-fetch
   └── 61× mcp_stdio_watchdog.py -- /root/.local/bin/uvx mcp-server-time
```

The watchdog count grew from 8 → 61 → 91 within minutes, indicating exponential spawning without backoff or rate limiting.

### Root Cause Chain
```
Gateway starts → discovers time/fetch MCP servers  
    ↓
Servers fail to start (broken/incompatible packages)
    ↓
mcp_stdio_watchdog.py enters revival loop (aggressive, no backoff)
    ↓
Each revival: uvx downloads from pypi.org → check_package_for_malware() → api.osv.dev
    ↓
Server still fails → loop continues → exponential growth (91 parallel watchdogs observed)
```

### Code Paths Involved

| File | Function | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `tools/mcp_stdio_watchdog.py` | main() | Spawns `uvx mcp-server-<name>` repeatedly |
| `hermes_cli/security_audit.py` | `check_package_for_malware()` | Calls `api.osv.dev/v1/querybatch` |
| `hermes_cli/security_audit.py` | `_osv_fetch_details()` | Calls `api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/` per finding |

## Impact

- **DNS flood:** ~13 queries/second sustained, ~47K/hour, saturating local DNS resolver
- **pypi.org abuse:** Continuous package downloads, 72K requests in 16h
- **api.osv.dev abuse:** 779K API queries — Google-hosted OSV infrastructure
- **CPU/memory:** 91 parallel Python watchdog processes consuming host resources
- **Discord latency:** Each hung MCP tool call blocks agent for 30-60s, causing 5+ minute response delays
- **Observability blind spot:** Only detectable with Pi-hole/DNS monitoring

## Environment

- Hermes v0.19.0 (v2026.7.20) on DietPi (native install, not Docker)
- Python 3.11, ~200 installed packages
- 22 MCP servers configured; `time` and `fetch` failed to start
- systemd service: `hermes-gateway.service`
- Pi-hole v6.4.3 as local DNS resolver

## Reproduction

1. Configure an MCP server that cannot start (e.g. `time` with incompatible dependencies)
2. Start Hermes gateway
3. Observe `mcp_stdio_watchdog.py` processes multiplying in `ps aux`
4. Check DNS logs for `api.osv.dev` and `pypi.org` traffic from Hermes host

## Workaround (Applied)

1. Wrapped `/root/.local/bin/uvx` with a shell script that rejects `mcp-server-time` and `mcp-server-fetch`:
   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   for arg in "$@"; do
       if [[ "$arg" == *mcp-server-time* ]] || [[ "$arg" == *mcp-server-fetch* ]]; then
           exit 1  # Fail fast — no network
       fi
   done
   exec /root/.local/bin/uvx.real "$@"
   ```
2. Restarted gateway to pick up wrapper
3. Failed servers now fail instantly without network calls

## Proposed Fixes

### Short-term (patch)
- Add exponential backoff to `mcp_stdio_watchdog.py` revival loop (max 3 attempts with increasing delay)
- Cap concurrent watchdog processes per MCP server
- Add `check_package_for_malware()` caching (don't re-query OSV for the same package in the same session)

### Long-term
- Gateway should permanently park MCP servers after N consecutive failures (not just 3, then retry)
- OSV/malware check should be async and non-blocking
- Consider an MCP health-check that doesn't require full package re-install

## Related

- #31460: feat(security): on-demand supply-chain audit via OSV.dev
- #29184: fix(mcp): run OSV malware preflight off the event loop
- #54794: Security audit OSV client reads response bodies without a cap
- #72108: v0.19.0 security audit reports High advisories

items.title: Make new session behavior predictable (Global New Chat vs Project New Session)

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Problem

As a Desktop user, I find it difficult to predict where a newly created session will belong.

Depending on the current workspace/CWD, a new session may appear under:

- the current project
- an auto project
- Home / detached

From the user's perspective this feels unpredictable.

## Suggested UX

The rules could be much simpler:

### Global "New Chat"
Always create a detached/Home session.

- Not attached to any project.
- Does not inherit the previous session's workspace.

### Project '+' button
Each project should have its own '+' button.

Creating a session from that button should always create a child session of that project, using the project's primary path as the initial workspace.

This gives users two very clear mental models:

- New Chat -> Home session
- Project + -> Session inside that project

No guessing.

## Why

The current workspace model is powerful, but project ownership becomes difficult to understand because session placement depends on internal workspace state instead of the UI action the user performed.

Predictable session creation would make Projects much easier to understand without changing the underlying workspace capabilities.

Thanks for considering it!

items.body:
## Environment
- OS: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045
- Hermes version: 0.17.0
- Username: l.marani (contains a dot)

## Problem
The bootstrap installer (install.ps1) fails repeatedly across multiple stages (
ode, system-packages, desktop) with this error:

> An object at the specified path C:\Users\L606E~1.MAR does not exist.

C:\Users\L606E~1.MAR is the Windows 8.3 short-name alias for C:\Users\l.marani (generated because the username contains a dot and is >8 chars).

The path IS accessible via PowerShell (Test-Path returns True) and via .NET APIs, so the 8.3 name exists on the filesystem. The failure happens in a post-operation verification step inside install.ps1 that uses the 8.3 short path in a Windows API context that does not resolve it.

## Log evidence

`
[OK] Node.js v22.23.2 installed to C:\Users\l.marani\AppData\Local\hermes\node\
[!] Portable Node.js download failed: An object at the specified path C:\Users\L606E~1.MAR does not exist.
`

`
{"skipped":false,"ok":false,"reason":"An object at the specified path C:\\Users\\L606E~1.MAR does not exist.","duration_ms":451220,"stage":"desktop"}
ERROR hermes_bootstrap_lib::bootstrap: bootstrap FAILED stage=Some("desktop") error=An object at the specified path C:\Users\L606E~1.MAR does not exist.
`

Note: the desktop build itself **succeeds** ([OK] Desktop app built, Hermes.exe created at 214 MB), but the post-build verification fails.

## Root cause hypothesis
install.ps1 calls a Windows API (possibly Shell COM or GetShortPathName) that returns the 8.3 form of the user profile path, then uses that short-form path in a subsequent check that fails. The fix is to always use the long-form path (from $env:USERPROFILE or similar) rather than any short-form conversion.

## Workaround
None found. system-packages stage passed on second retry; desktop stage did not.

items.title: Feature request: add an option to disable secret masking to stop agent auto-fixes

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
Summary
The agent currently redacts secrets and potential tokens in outputs and logs by replacing them with ***. However, when the agent inspects files via CLI tools (grep, read_file, etc.), the display-layer masking makes the agent believe that *** literally exists in the source files as syntax errors or malformed code.

This causes the agent to enter loop behavior—attempting automatic "fixes" (writing raw Python scripts, patching files, checking hex bytes) to remove what it perceives as broken code on disk.

Real-World Case Study
During a code refactoring session, the agent ran standard code inspection tools.

False Alarm: The agent read output containing requiresApiKey: *** and assumed *** was literally written to the configuration source file.

Wasted Execution Steps: Believing the code was broken, the agent generated scripts to byte-patch the files on disk to replace *** with actual logical variables.

Confusion & Discovery: The project's linter/static analyzer passed with zero errors. The agent only realized the code on disk was intact after running a raw Hex byte inspection, confirming that *** was merely an artifact added by the agent's display redaction layer.

This loop wasted substantial execution time, context window, and API tokens.

Problem Breakdown
Agent Misinterpretation: Masked values like *** or truncated tokens returned by stdout/logs trigger automated repair routines (write_file, patching, refactoring).

Disruptive Auto-fixes: Developers intentionally working with mock values, placeholder tokens, or local API credentials face unintended code modifications.

Global Enforcement: Redaction is currently applied unconditionally at display/logging time without a mechanism to opt out in trusted local environments.

Proposed Solution
Introduce an explicit toggle (environment variable or configuration key) to disable runtime display redaction so the agent sees raw values and refrains from "fixing" masked display artifacts.

Implementation Details
Environment Variable / Config:

Default: HERMES_REDACT_ENABLED=1 (Masking enabled).

Opt-out: HERMES_REDACT_ENABLED=0 or false (Bypasses redaction in the helper and returns raw strings).

Helper Hook:

Integrate the flag into the core redaction function (agent/redact.py::mask_secret).

Documentation & Security Warning:

Document HERMES_REDACT_ENABLED in README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.

Add a clear note that disabling redaction may expose sensitive data in local logs and UI.

(Optional) CLI Warning:

Show a single cautionary warning on launch when HERMES_REDACT_ENABLED=0 is active.

Example Usage
Bash
# Temporarily disable display redaction for local debugging
export HERMES_REDACT_ENABLED=0

# Run Hermes
hermes chat -q "Refactor configuration parser"
Why This Helps
Prevents Redaction Loops: Stops the agent from misinterpreting *** in display outputs as syntax errors.

Saves Time & Tokens: Eliminates unnecessary byte-inspection scripts and redundant file patching.

Empowers Power Users: Offers an explicit escape hatch for local development while preserving default server-side security.

items.title: [Bug]: delegate_task summary budget uses cumulative session_prompt_tokens → batch summaries always trimmed to 2000-char floor on long sessions

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

`_parent_summary_char_budget()` in `tools/delegate_tool.py` computes the dynamic per-summary cap using `parent_agent.session_prompt_tokens` as "current context usage". But `session_prompt_tokens` is a **session-cumulative lifetime counter** (`agent_init.py:2582` sets it to 0; `conversation_loop.py:3195` and `codex_runtime.py:134` do `+=` per API call; it is **never reset**, not even after context compression). On any long-lived session the cumulative value dwarfs `context_length`, so `headroom_tokens` is permanently negative and every batch summary is trimmed down to the `_MIN_SUMMARY_CHARS = 2000` floor — regardless of how small the live context actually is.

## Evidence

- `agent_init.py:2582` — `agent.session_prompt_tokens = 0`
- `conversation_loop.py:3195` — `agent.session_prompt_tokens += prompt_tokens` (per API call, cumulative)
- `conversation_compression.py` / `context_compressor.py` — no code path ever resets `session_prompt_tokens`
- `delegate_tool.py:1972` — `used_tokens = getattr(parent_agent, "session_prompt_tokens", 0)` used as "what's already in its prompt" (docstring line 1958-1959)

Real-world impact: in the past 7 days, 262 messages in the local session DB carry `[SUMMARY TRUNCATED]` (13-64 per day). A 3,198-char subagent summary was trimmed to 1,457 head + 498 tail while the parent's live context was ~50K tokens of a 256K window — truncation triggered by the cumulative counter, not by actual context pressure.

The correct value exists: `context_compressor.last_prompt_tokens` (`context_compressor.py:2285`, updated from the latest real provider `prompt_tokens` on every response; `last_real_prompt_tokens` survives compression boundaries).

## Suggested fix

In `_parent_summary_char_budget()`, prefer `compressor.last_prompt_tokens` (falling back to `last_real_prompt_tokens`, then `session_prompt_tokens`):

```python
used_tokens = getattr(compressor, "last_prompt_tokens", 0) or 0
if not isinstance(used_tokens, (int, float)) or used_tokens <= 0:
    used_tokens = getattr(compressor, "last_real_prompt_tokens", 0) or 0
if not isinstance(used_tokens, (int, float)) or used_tokens <= 0:
    used_tokens = getattr(parent_agent, "session_prompt_tokens", 0)
if not isinstance(used_tokens, (int, float)) or used_tokens < 0:
    used_tokens = 0
```

The static `delegation.max_summary_chars` ceiling and the `_MIN_SUMMARY_CHARS` floor are unchanged, so this cannot flip the behavior from over-trimming to context overflow.

## Related

- #9126 introduced the summary-budget mechanism (the bug is an incorrect-metric variant of it)
- #70204 — same root cause (`session_prompt_tokens` cumulative semantics) misused in the ACP adapter

items.body:
# v0.19.1 in-app Update still loops on Windows despite #75498 being closed as fixed

## Summary

`#75498` (Windows "Hermes is still running" loop on in-app Update) was closed as "not planned" by `teknium1` with the comment that v0.19.1 ships the fix in commit `8c76fe19f80c96c1a462147c447a7666b826dd2d` (passed `HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID` to the child `hermes update` process so it can recognize the parent-held marker). I just rebuilt the Hermes.exe binary from the `v2026.7.30` tag (`cc4cab2f592e60a197e796506de9168f74baf3ea`) and the loop is still there. Either the fix is incomplete or it doesn't cover the actual scenario the loop hits on Windows.

## Why this is a new issue, not a comment on #75498

`#75498` was closed as "not planned" 30 min before I posted my first technical comment there. The closing rationale — "the reported self-lock/retry loop is already fixed on main and shipped in v2026.7.30 (v0.19.1)" — is now testable, and the test fails. I think this warrants its own issue that explicitly asks the maintainer to re-open #75498 or ship a real fix, rather than slipping it in as a comment on a closed issue.

## Reproduction (fresh install, no operational corruption)

- **OS**: Windows 11 Pro 24H2, no WSL involvement
- **Hermes version installed**: v0.19.1 (`source: "local"` after the rebuild — see below)
- **Install state**: clean. No leftover `.hermes-update-in-progress`, no zombie `node.exe` / `hermes-setup.exe` from prior interrupted updates, no stale `__gui.lock`/`.update_check`. The user's prior two-night loop was caused by a mid-update reboot; this is a separate, clean reproduction.
- **Source commit on disk**: `cc4cab2f5` (annotated tag `v2026.7.30`, the v0.19.1 release tip)
- **Binary on disk**: `apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/Hermes.exe`, mtime 2026-07-31T17:32Z, freshly built via `npm run build` + `npm run pack` against the `v2026.7.30` source (NOT a CI build; the local installer I tried earlier clobbered the v0.19.1 checkout, so I built the binary manually).
- **Fix presence check**: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 8c76fe19f80c96c1a462147c447a7666b826dd2d HEAD` → **exit 0**. The fix commit is in the source the binary was built from. So the loop is NOT due to a missing fix; it's a real failure of the fix as-shipped.

## What actually happens (log evidence, this session)

User clicks **Update** in the desktop while local source is at `cc4cab2f` and `origin/main` is at `afc54ca8` (so Update button shows "many commits behind"). Within 4 seconds:

**`bootstrap-installer.log` (verbatim, relevant lines only):**
```
2026-07-31T17:32:... INFO hermes_bootstrap_lib: Hermes installer starting mode=Update force_setup=false
2026-07-31T17:32:... INFO bootstrap.log: [update] waiting for Hermes to exit… stage=update
2026-07-31T17:32:... INFO bootstrap.log: [update] updating against branch main stage=update
2026-07-31T17:32:... INFO hermes_bootstrap_lib::update: update stage stage=update state=Running
2026-07-31T17:32:... INFO bootstrap.log: ✗ Another Hermes update is already running (PID <wrapper>, started 4s ago). stage=update
2026-07-31T17:32:... INFO bootstrap.log:   Two updates mutating the same checkout corrupt it: one rewrites
2026-07-31T17:32:... INFO bootstrap.log:   source while the other is mid-install. Wait for it to finish, or
2026-07-31T17:32:... INFO bootstrap.log:   close the window/dashboard tab that started it, then retry.
2026-07-31T17:32:... INFO hermes_bootstrap_lib::update: update stage stage=update state=Failed
                                          error=Some("Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again.")
```

**Desktop UI (verbatim):** red "UPDATE DIDN'T FINISH" header, "Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again." sub-text, blue **Retry update** button, gray **Open log folder** button, log path label `Log: C:\Users\r3dp0\AppData\Local\hermes\logs\bootstrap-installer.log`.

**Lock file created at the moment of the click, then never cleaned up:**
```
$ od -c 'C:\Users\r3dp0\AppData\Local\hermes\.hermes-update-in-progress'
0000000   2   1   3   7   2  \n   1   7   8   5   5   1   2   3   4   2  \n
```
(PID + started_at_unix — the exact format described in the Rust `UpdateMarkerGuard` doc comment.)

**Process tree immediately after the click:**
- Desktop (`Hermes.exe` PID, e.g. `10052`) — quit cleanly per `applyUpdates` ("exiting desktop to release venv shim")
  - `hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main` (e.g. PID `21372`) — wrote the lock, started
    - `msedgewebview2.exe` (PID `5960`) — Tauri webview, child of `21372`

So the installer's wrapper is alive, the lock has the wrapper's PID, the wrapper reads the lock, and the comment's promise — "Self-PID is treated as non-ownership on purpose (#74761)" — does **not** fire. Identical symptom to what the original `teknium1` comment on #75498 calls "fixed" in `8c76fe19`.

## Why the shipped fix doesn't work here (hypothesis)

`8c76fe19` passes `HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID` to a child `hermes update` process, so the *Python* child can recognize the parent's marker. In the Windows Tauri build, the wrapper `hermes-setup.exe` is itself a Tauri app (the user sees a Tauri WebView window), and the actual update logic appears to run inside that same Tauri process, not in a separate `hermes update` Python child. So:
- The marker gets written by the Tauri wrapper (PID `21372`)
- The Tauri wrapper is also the process that *reads* the marker
- `std::process::id()` in the Rust side IS `21372` (verified via wmic), so the `if pid == std::process::id() { return None; }` line at `update.rs:163-165` *should* fire
- It doesn't. Error message shows PID `21372` (self). The function returns `Some(MarkerOwner)`.

That points to a Tauri-runtime quirk — possibly the Tauri async runtime is reading the marker in a context where `std::process::id()` reports something other than the wrapper's actual OS PID (e.g. Tauri re-execs `hermes-setup.exe` under a new PID for the actual update, and the marker was written by the old shell). The `pid_is_alive` check at line 158 would correctly see the original wrapper as alive, and the self-PID comparison at line 163 would correctly fail because the comparison is happening in the inner process with a different PID. The result: the comment's intent (own-PID adoption) does not survive the Tauri shell indirection.

## Cross-checks against what was already filed

- **#74942** "Desktop app updater detects itself as 'another instance' running (false positive on PID check)" — same symptom, different (older) install. Still open. **This new report is the v0.19.1 version of that bug.**
- **#74531** (macOS) — same idea, macOS path, still open.
- **#75278** "Tauri updater handoff fails on macOS — HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID mismatch" — describes exactly the Tauri-runtime handoff problem on macOS that I think is the actual root cause on Windows too. Still open.

## What the user (me) is doing about it locally

Renaming `Local\hermes\hermes-agent\.git` to `.git.disabled`. That makes `checkUpdates()` short-circuit to `{ supported: false, reason: 'not-a-git-checkout' }` and the in-app Update button is no longer rendered. The user keeps the v0.19.1 binary; future frontend updates come from re-running `Hermes-Setup.exe` manually. Backend Update button (separate code path) is unaffected.

## Suggested next steps (for the maintainers)

1. Re-open #75498 and #74761 — both were closed "not planned" with the v0.19.1 fix claim; the fix doesn't actually work.
2. Either (a) extend the self-PID exclusion to *also* include the immediate parent process PID (so the Tauri-shell case is covered), or (b) have the Tauri wrapper write the marker with `process.ppid` rather than its own `child.pid`, or (c) log `std::process::id()` + lock PID + comparison result inside `live_marker_owner` so the failure mode is visible when the next person hits it.
3. A regression test that exercises the Tauri-shell wrapper → installer spawn path on Windows specifically (the existing `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_lock.py:181` covers the Python child case but not the Tauri wrapper case).

## How to repro in 5 minutes (on Windows)

```powershell
# from a fresh v0.19.1 install (Hermes-Setup.exe ran clean)
cd $env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\hermes-agent
git checkout v2026.7.30
cd apps/desktop
npm install
npm run build
npm run pack
# relaunch Hermes, click Update, watch bootstrap-installer.log
```

If you have the v0.19.1 install from the standard `Hermes-Setup.exe` flow (the v0.19.1 release page has no prebuilt `Hermes-Setup.exe` assets; the CI image that ships is main HEAD, not v0.19.1), the symptom reproduces there too with whatever happens to be the latest main commit. The bug isn't tagged to a single commit.

## Cross-link

First technical report is in the comment thread on **#75498**, where the maintainer closed the issue as "not planned" and cited `8c76fe19` as the shipped fix.

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary
Telegram gateway hangs indefinitely at "Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…" 
even though the watchdog/timeout fixes from #67498, e16743b0d, d50aae0e3, and 
9f0309504 are all present in this version. strace shows a successful TCP 
connection and TLS handshake to a Telegram DC, but the adapter never 
progresses past attempt 1.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (2026.7.30) · upstream 8f8bee94
- Python 3.11.15 (venv)
- Install method: git
- OS: Ubuntu (Dell Latitude 5520 laptop)
- Gateway run as systemd --user service (also reproduces in foreground `hermes gateway`)

## Steps already ruled out
- Network/DNS: `curl -I https://api.telegram.org` and direct httpx calls succeed immediately
- No HTTP/HTTPS proxy set (`env | grep -i proxy` empty)
- IPv6 disabled system-wide via sysctl — no change
- TELEGRAM_FALLBACK_IPS set explicitly (skips DoH discovery step, confirmed 
  by its log line disappearing) — hang still occurs at attempt 1/8
- Token and TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS confirmed correctly set (uncommented, 
  correct format)
- Confirmed via `git log` that commits 733830980, e16743b0d, d50aae0e3, 
  9f0309504 are all present in this branch/version

## strace evidence (attached process 36758, foreground `hermes gateway`)
Key lines showing a completed TCP connect + active TLS handshake to a 
Telegram DC IP from TELEGRAM_FALLBACK_IPS:

    getpeername(17, ..., sin_addr=inet_addr("149.154.166.110")) = 0
    recvfrom(17, "\27\3\3\1\260\242\372...", 262144, 0, NULL, NULL) = 437
    sendto(17, "\27\3\3\1L\331\312\340...", 337, 0, NULL, 0) = 337
    sendto(17, "\27\3\3\2\201n\336\301...", 646, 0, NULL, 0) = 646

This looks like a TLS 1.3 ClientHello/Certificate/Finished exchange 
completing normally at the socket level. No further progress is logged 
by the adapter afterward — no "attempt 2/8", no timeout error, no 
success message.

## Also observed
- On every gateway stop/restart cycle: 
  `ERROR hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Failed to 
  send Telegram message: Chat not found` — possibly a separate issue 
  related to the home-channel shutdown/startup notification.

## Request
Given the TLS handshake completes at the socket level but the adapter 
never reports success or moves to a retry, this suggests the post-TLS 
application-layer response parsing (or Application.initialize() completion 
callback) may be what's actually stalling — possibly a regression 
introduced alongside the #67498 watchdog logic, or an edge case the 
watchdog doesn't cover (e.g., a stalled getMe() call after connect).

items.title: [Feature]: Support Client ID Metadata Documents and configurable token-request User-Agent for MCP OAuth

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Hermes' native OAuth support for HTTP MCP servers does not currently expose two interoperability capabilities supported or required by some OAuth authorization servers:

1. **Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD)**  
   The MCP Python SDK's `OAuthClientProvider` accepts a `client_metadata_url`. When an authorization server advertises `client_id_metadata_document_supported=true`, the SDK can use that HTTPS metadata URL as the client ID instead of performing Dynamic Client Registration.

   Hermes currently does not propagate this option through either `build_oauth_auth()` or `MCPOAuthManager`, so the SDK cannot select its CIMD path. Servers that support CIMD but do not accept Hermes' fallback registration flow cannot complete authentication.

2. **An explicit User-Agent for token requests**  
   Some authorization servers or network protection layers reject the default HTTP library User-Agent on the token endpoint. Hermes has no per-server way to set an explicit User-Agent on authorization-code exchange and refresh-token requests.

This is a generic MCP OAuth interoperability gap and does not require any server-specific behavior.

Verified against current `origin/main` at `6ecd335aa897e9765fc5c4d02b2f74b2d1e2c781`.

### Proposed Solution

Add two optional fields to the existing per-server OAuth configuration:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  example:
    url: "https://mcp.example.com/mcp"
    auth: oauth
    oauth:
      client_metadata_url: "https://client.example/oauth/client-metadata"
      user_agent: "My-MCP-Client/1.0"
```

Expected behavior:

- Pass `client_metadata_url` to the MCP SDK's `OAuthClientProvider`.
- Let the SDK perform its existing validation and CIMD capability check.
- When CIMD is supported, use the metadata URL as the client ID and skip Dynamic Client Registration.
- Apply `user_agent` only to token endpoint requests:
  - authorization-code exchange
  - refresh-token exchange
- Accept only a non-empty string for `user_agent`.
- Preserve existing behavior when either option is absent or null.
- Keep both options explicitly per-server and opt-in.
- Do not add arbitrary token headers or any server-specific branches.

Suggested acceptance criteria:

- All active OAuth provider-construction paths propagate `client_metadata_url`.
- The actual SDK `async_auth_flow` selects CIMD when the authorization server advertises support.
- Both authorization-code and refresh-token requests carry the configured User-Agent.
- Missing, empty, or null `user_agent` values do not add a header.
- Existing Dynamic Client Registration and pre-registered client flows remain unchanged.
- Documentation covers both options and notes that the metadata URL must satisfy the SDK's HTTPS validation.
- Flow-level tests use real provider imports and a temporary `HERMES_HOME`, not only mocked constructor assertions.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Dynamic Client Registration:** Not equivalent; some authorization servers support CIMD but do not accept the fallback registration flow.
- **A fixed `client_id`:** Does not represent a Client ID Metadata Document and bypasses the SDK's CIMD negotiation.
- **Arbitrary token-request headers:** Broader than necessary and increases the risk of accidentally placing secrets in configuration.
- **A local monkeypatch or core overlay:** Works as a temporary workaround but is fragile across Hermes updates and duplicates generic OAuth behavior outside the supported configuration surface.

### Feature Type

Configuration option

### Scope

Medium (few files, under 300 lines including tests and documentation)

Likely areas:

- `tools/mcp_oauth.py`
- `tools/mcp_oauth_manager.py`
- MCP OAuth unit and integration tests
- MCP configuration documentation

### Contribution

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

A local proof of concept already exercises the real SDK auth-flow generator through CIMD and token exchange, verifies the User-Agent on code and refresh requests, and passes the targeted MCP OAuth test suite. It can be prepared as a PR after maintainers confirm the configuration shape.

items.title: [Bug] Short tool-only suffix can make context compressor scan past messages

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

A short conversation whose protected head/tool grouping reaches the end of the message list can make `_find_tail_cut_by_tokens()` return `len(messages) + 1`. `compress()` then passes that value into `_find_latest_context_summary()` / `_find_context_summaries()`, which indexes `messages[idx]` without clamping and raises `IndexError`.

This escapes the compression path and fails the active gateway turn.

## Observed failure

Hermes Agent `v2026.7.7.2`, Discord gateway, compressor engine enabled:

```text
context compression started: messages=8
agent/context_compressor.py:2808 in compress
  _find_latest_context_summary(messages, summary_search_start, compress_end)
agent/context_compressor.py:2189 in _find_latest_context_summary
  content = messages[idx].get("content")
IndexError: list index out of range
```

The reproduced internal bounds were:

```text
len(messages) = 8
compress_start = 8
compress_end = 9
```

The transcript ended in a tool-call/result group. `_align_boundary_forward()` moved the protected start to the end of the list. `_find_tail_cut_by_tokens()` then applied the forward-progress floor `head_end + 1`, producing 9 even though the only valid exclusive end is 8.

## Current source

The exact line moved in newer releases, but the defect remains present in `v2026.7.30` and current `main`: `_find_context_summaries()` iterates `range(start, end)` and indexes `messages[idx]` without bounding either value. The latest tail-cut implementation can still return an index past `len(messages)` when `head_end >= len(messages)`.

This is distinct from #59496 / #70251, which handle an empty post-handoff summary window but do not bound an out-of-range end index.

## Expected behavior

Compression must never raise for a valid message list. When alignment leaves no compressible middle (`head_end >= len(messages)`), tail cut should return `len(messages)` and `compress()` should take its existing no-compressible-window path.

Summary scanning should also defensively clamp `start` and `end` to `[0, len(messages)]` and tolerate non-dict rows rather than indexing out of bounds.

## Suggested regression coverage

1. Eight-message live-shaped transcript ending in an assistant tool call plus tool results; aligned head equals `len(messages)`; assert `compress()` returns without raising.
2. Direct summary scan with `end > len(messages)`; assert it scans only existing rows.
3. `start < 0`, `start > end`, empty messages, and a malformed/non-dict row; assert fail-safe behavior.
4. Assert `_find_tail_cut_by_tokens(messages, head_end=len(messages)) == len(messages)`.

No message should be removed and no summary model should be called when there is no compressible window.

items.title: [Bug]: v0.19.1 primary Anthropic path routes to /chat/completions with placeholder Bearer, ignores console API key

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
# Hermes v0.19.1 — Anthropic Requests Silently Downgraded to /chat/completions Shim

## Summary

On macOS 15.6, Hermes v0.19.1 (upstream 5835201d, install method: git) routes
every Anthropic request through the OpenAI-compat `/chat/completions` shim on
`https://api.anthropic.com/` with an `Authorization: Bearer <11-char placeholder>`
header, regardless of what's in the credential pool. The native
`/v1/messages` route is never used, even though every configuration and
mode-selection function in the CLI's own code returns the correct
`anthropic_messages` transport for `api.anthropic.com`.

The user-visible symptom is an HTTP 400 "You're out of extra usage. Add more at
claude.ai/settings/usage" that is misleading — the shim silently accounts against
a subscription-billed extra-usage pool while the account's Console API balance
sits untouched. This exact failure mode is even documented in v0.19.1's own
source (`hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py:107-114`), but the mandatory-override
fix at `model_switch.py:1636` does not fire on this machine.

## Version + platform

```
Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (2026.7.30) · upstream 5835201d
Install directory: /Users/USER/.hermes/hermes-agent
Install method: git
Python: 3.11.15
OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0
Up to date
```

- macOS: 15.7.4
- Python: 3.11.15 (Hermes venv)
- anthropic SDK: 0.87.0
- openai SDK: 2.24.0

## Credential pool (labels/types only — no secrets)
```
anthropic (1 credentials):
  #1  console-prepaid      api_key manual exhausted invalid_request_error (400) (59m 11s left)

```

## Relevant `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (no secrets by design)
```yaml
model:
  default: claude-sonnet-5
  provider: anthropic
providers: null
terminal:
  backend: local
  cwd: /Users/USER/Desktop/git-repos/<user-project>
```

## In-process code verification (mode selection IS correct at definition time)

```
get_provider("anthropic").transport = anthropic_messages
host_mandated_api_mode("https://api.anthropic.com") = anthropic_messages
determine_api_mode("anthropic", "https://api.anthropic.com") = anthropic_messages
```

All three return `anthropic_messages`. Yet the actual HTTP request uses the OpenAI-compat shim.

## Minimal reproducer command (fully isolated)

```bash
hermes chat -q "AUTH_OK_TEST" -Q \
  --provider anthropic \
  --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 \
  --safe-mode \
  --ignore-user-config \
  --ignore-rules \
  --max-turns 3 \
  --source repro
```

`--safe-mode --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules` guarantees no user config
or memory injection can be a factor. The bug persists.

## Actual HTTP request (verified from ~/.hermes/sessions/request_dump_*.json)

```
url:               https://api.anthropic.com/chat/completions   ← wrong path
                                                                  (native Messages API is /v1/messages)
method:            POST
Authorization:     Bearer <4-char placeholder>                   ← wrong auth
                                                                  (correct: x-api-key: sk-ant-... [108 chars])
x-api-key:         <empty>                                       ← header not sent
Content-Type:      application/json
body.model:        claude-sonnet-5
```

## What was tried, all with the identical broken result

| # | Invocation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `hermes -z PROMPT --provider anthropic` via project runner | broken |
| 2 | `hermes chat -q QUERY -Q --provider anthropic --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` | broken |
| 3 | Same as #2 without `--provider` flag (auto-detect) | broken |
| 4 | Same but with `--safe-mode --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules` (fully isolated) | broken |
| 5 | After `hermes config set model.base_url https://api.anthropic.com` | broken |
| 6 | After `hermes config set model.api_mode anthropic_messages` | broken |
| 7 | After interactive `hermes model` re-selection (Anthropic → claude-sonnet-5, native Messages) | broken |
| 8 | After `hermes auth reset anthropic` between each attempt (clears local exhausted flag) | broken |
| 9 | Verified fresh credential added via `hermes auth add anthropic --type api-key --label console-prepaid` (108-char sk-ant-...) | broken (secret never sent) |

## Documented failure mode in the CLI's own source

`hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py` lines 107-114 (v0.19.1) documents this exact symptom:

> Direct api.anthropic.com endpoints must use the native Messages API (`/v1/messages`).
> Anthropic also exposes an OpenAI-compat `/chat/completions` shim on the same host,
> but Pro/Max OAuth subscriptions are only billed against the native Messages route;
> hitting the shim accounts against a separate "extra usage" pool that is empty by
> default and surfaces as HTTP 400 "You're out of extra usage." See issue #32243.

The intended fix at `hermes_cli/model_switch.py:1636` calls
`host_mandated_api_mode(base_url)` and unconditionally overrides the mode when the
host mandates one. That code path apparently does not execute for our
`chat -q` + `-z` invocation forms on this machine.

## Expected

Request goes to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` with `x-api-key: sk-ant-...` and completes.

## Actual

Request goes to `https://api.anthropic.com/chat/completions` with a placeholder `Bearer` token and returns HTTP 400 with a misleading subscription-usage message.

## Impact

All non-interactive Anthropic model calls through Hermes are broken on this install. The user's Console API balance and console-prepaid credential are not consumed at all — Hermes never sends the key.

## Bug Description

On Windows, the WhatsApp gateway flashes **visible console windows** (hosted by Windows Terminal) during bridge reconnect cycles. Each flash lasts ~150 ms: the console window appears and closes immediately, repeatedly, while the gateway is running — very distracting during normal use.

The gateway runs headless under `pythonw.exe` (no console). Any console-subsystem child it spawns **without** `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` forces Windows to allocate a new console, which — with Windows Terminal set as the default terminal application — pops a visible WT window for the lifetime of the child (~80–150 ms for these fast commands).

## Evidence (event-driven window hook)

I instrumented the machine with a `SetWinEventHook` watcher (`EVENT_OBJECT_CREATE/SHOW/HIDE` on `ConsoleWindowClass`/`CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS`) and caught the flashes live:

```
16:47:16.469  NEW node.exe --version          (parent: pythonw gateway)
16:47:16.935  **CONSOLE-WINDOW SHOW** (Windows Terminal)   <- flash 1
16:47:17.573  **CONSOLE-WINDOW SHOW** (Windows Terminal)   <- flash 2
16:47:20.699  NEW node.exe bridge.js --port 3000 (parent: pythonw gateway)
16:47:25.557  bridge exits
16:47:26.620  taskkill /PID <bridge> /T       (parent: pythonw gateway)
16:47:26.178  **CONSOLE-WINDOW SHOW** (Windows Terminal)   <- flash 3
16:47:26.725  **CONSOLE-WINDOW HIDE** title='C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\taskkill.exe'
```

All three flashes map to exactly three subprocess call sites in `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py` that lack the window-hiding flag.

## Root Cause

Three spawns in `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py` run without `creationflags` on Windows (the gateway is a windowless `pythonw.exe` parent, so each one allocates a visible console):

1. **`_terminate_bridge_process()`** — `taskkill /PID <pid> /T` (fires on every bridge terminate: reconnect cycles, shutdown, crash recovery)
2. **`check_whatsapp_requirements()`** — `node --version` (fires on every bridge start / reconnect attempt)
3. **WhatsAppAdapter bridge-dependency setup** — `npm install --silent` (fires when bridge deps are (re)installed)

Note the bridge spawn itself (`windows_detach_popen_kwargs()`) and `_kill_port_process()` (`netstat`/`taskkill` with `windows_hide_flags()`) were already correct — only these three sites were missed.

## Fix Applied

Add `creationflags=windows_hide_flags() if _IS_WINDOWS else 0` to the three calls (the flag is a no-op on POSIX). Verified: after restarting the gateway with the patch, the same `taskkill`/`node --version` calls run with **zero** window events in the hook log.

index 3881502e5d..84470d0340 100644
--- a/hermes_cli/clipboard.py

@@ -19,6 +19,7 @@ import subprocess

@@ -121,6 +123,7 @@ def write_clipboard_text(text: str) -> bool:

## Environment

items.title: [Bug]: sqlite_safe_read untracks a connection before closing it, so a failed close leaves the byte-probe guard believing nothing is live

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug description

`TrackedConnection.close()` decrements the live-connection registry **before** performing the real close, and does not undo that decrement when the close fails. A failed close therefore leaves the descriptor open while `has_live_connection()` reports that nothing is live.

```python
# hermes_cli/sqlite_safe_read.py — TrackedConnection / _TrackingMixin
def close(self) -> None:
    with _live_lock:
        path = getattr(self, "_hermes_tracked_path", None)
        if path is not None:
            self._hermes_tracked_path = None
            untrack_connection(path)     # <-- registry decremented first
        super().close()                  # <-- may raise; decrement is not undone
```

This is not a hypothetical failure path. Per #74304, per-thread read connections are created with the default `check_same_thread=True`, so *every* cross-thread drain in `SessionDB.close()` raises `sqlite3.ProgrammingError` — and every caller wraps `conn.close()` in a bare `except`. The registry has therefore been under-counting systematically wherever a reader was closed from a thread other than its owner.

## Why this matters beyond the fd count

`read_header_bytes_preopen()` is gated entirely on that registry:

```python
with _live_lock:
    if not force and _key(path) in _live_connections:
        ...
        return None          # refuse the byte-level read
```

Once the count is wrongly zero, the guard permits a byte-level `open()`/`read()`/`close()` on a database that this process still holds open. That `close()` cancels **every POSIX advisory lock the process holds on the file** — which this module's own docstring correctly identifies as the documented route to `database disk image is malformed`:

> the close() system call will cancel all POSIX advisory locks on the same file for all threads and all file descriptors in the process

So the module can be talked out of the exact protection it exists to provide. It also means the registry cannot be trusted as leak instrumentation: a leaked-but-failed-close connection is invisible to it.

## Reproduction

Against pristine `main` (`b1858f33`), Python 3.11.15, macOS:

```python
import threading, tempfile, os, sqlite3, subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from hermes_cli.sqlite_safe_read import (
    connect_tracked, has_live_connection, read_header_bytes_preopen)

d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); db = d / "state.db"
c0 = sqlite3.connect(db); c0.execute("create table t(x)"); c0.commit(); c0.close()

pid = os.getpid()
def fds():
    out = subprocess.run(["lsof", "-p", str(pid)], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    return sum(1 for l in out.splitlines() if str(db) in l)

box = {}
t = threading.Thread(target=lambda: box.update(c=connect_tracked(db)))
t.start(); t.join()                      # owner thread has now exited

print(fds(), has_live_connection(db))    # 1 True
try:
    box["c"].close()                     # the cross-thread drain
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__)              # ProgrammingError — callers swallow this

print(fds())                             # 1   <- descriptor STILL open
print(has_live_connection(db))           # False <- registry says nothing is live
print(read_header_bytes_preopen(db) is not None)   # True <- guard now permits the probe
```

Output:

```text
opened on a worker thread, which has now exited
  real descriptors on the file : 1
  has_live_connection()        : True
  close() raised               : ProgrammingError (swallowed by callers)

AFTER the failed cross-thread close:
  real descriptors on the file : 1      <-- STILL OPEN
  has_live_connection()        : False  <-- registry now says nothing is live
  byte-probe guard permits read: True   <-- will open+close a LIVE db
```

## Expected behavior

- The registry entry is released only when the descriptor is actually gone.
- A `close()` that raises leaves the connection tracked, so `has_live_connection()` keeps reporting it and the byte-probe guard keeps refusing.
- The check and the state change remain within one `_live_lock` critical section, so a concurrent probe still cannot observe a torn state.

## Proposed minimal fix

Invert the order inside the existing critical section:

```python
def close(self) -> None:
    with _live_lock:
        path = getattr(self, "_hermes_tracked_path", None)
        # Close FIRST, untrack only once it actually succeeded.
        super().close()
        if path is not None:
            self._hermes_tracked_path = None
            untrack_connection(path)
```

Still one critical section, so the ordering guarantee in the module docstring is preserved. If `super().close()` raises, the exception propagates exactly as before — callers that already swallow it are unaffected — but the registry now stays correct.

A regression test worth adding: assert that a `close()` which raises leaves `has_live_connection()` true and `read_header_bytes_preopen()` refusing.

## Relationship to #74304 and #75269

Complementary, and all three want to land together:

- **#75269** — readers from finished threads are never reaped. Governs how *many* connections reach a failing close.
- **#74304** — `check_same_thread=False` so the drain can actually close them. Removes the most common source of the failing close.
- **This issue** — the registry must not decrement when a close fails. Independent of both: after #74304 the cross-thread `ProgrammingError` largely goes away, but any other close failure (I/O error, already-closed, a caller-supplied factory) still corrupts the count, and the guard is a corruption-safety mechanism rather than bookkeeping.

Fixing only #74304 hides this rather than resolving it.

## Environment

- hermes-agent 0.19.0 @ `b1858f33a1cc6083ee34aea41417ea5e18564d2e`
- Python 3.11.15, macOS 25.5.0
- Found while chasing a dashboard fd exhaustion (`API call failed after 3 retries: [Errno 24] Too many open files`); the under-counting registry is why the leak was invisible to the very instrumentation meant to surface it.
