items.title: [Bug]: tool_search never indexes HA-Assist-native custom-script MCP tools, even in fresh sessions
items.body:
## Bug Description

`tool_search` (progressive-disclosure bridge, default `tools.tool_search: auto`) appears to
never index a specific class of MCP tools: ones dynamically exposed via Home Assistant's native
Assist LLM API (i.e., user-created HA scripts with `expose to Assist` enabled, bridged into the
MCP catalog under a `<backend>__<script_key>` name). These tools are reachable and callable
directly (`tool_call` with the exact name works fine, and `tool_describe` resolves them), but
`tool_search` never surfaces them — not even with an exact-substring query and a generous
`limit`, on a **fresh session** (no mid-session catalog change involved, so this looks distinct
from #72560's stale-refresh issue).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register at least one Home-Assistant-native-Assist-exposed script as an MCP tool alongside a
   normal fixed-surface MCP backend (in our case: an MCP backend exposing both a generic HA
   REST-API surface — `get_state`, `list_entities`, `get_history`, ... — and several
   HA-Assist-native custom scripts, e.g. `<backend>__mcp_get_house_reference` and
   `<backend>__mcp_get_entity_history`). Total catalog size in our case: 197 tools.
2. Start a **fresh** Hermes session (`hermes -z ... --cli --yolo`), `tools.tool_search.enabled:
   auto` (default), no prior mid-session tool changes.
3. Ask the model to call `tool_search` with the exact tool name as the query, e.g.
   `query="mcp_get_entity_history", limit=50`.
4. Observe: 20 results returned, all from the fixed REST-API surface
   (`get_history`/`get_logbook`/`get_statistics`/`get_state`/...) — the actual target tool never
   appears.
5. Repeat with `limit=200` (> total catalog size of 197) and an even more targeted query
   (`get_house_reference`, exact tool-name substring) for a second, different HA-Assist-native
   tool (`<backend>__mcp_get_house_reference`) — still zero hits across 18 varied queries in one
   session (substrings, synonyms, `source=mcp`/`source=custom` filters, limits 5→200).
6. Confirm the tool genuinely exists and is well-described: `tool_describe` on the exact name
   resolves fine, and the underlying HA script config has a clear alias + description (verified
   directly via the HA API, not just via Hermes) — so this isn't a naming/description-quality
   issue.
7. Confirm the workaround: setting `tools.tool_search.enabled: off` (direct/eager tool exposure,
   bypassing the bridge entirely) makes the same tool immediately usable by the same model in the
   same session type.

## Expected Behavior

`tool_search` should index the complete deferred-tool catalog, including MCP tools that
originate from a host application's own dynamic tool-exposure mechanism (here: Home Assistant's
Assist LLM API surfacing user-exposed scripts as individual MCP tools), not just a fixed/static
subset of the backend.

## Actual Behavior

A specific, real, well-described, callable tool is never returned by `tool_search`, regardless of
query specificity or `limit`, even in a fresh session with no mid-session catalog churn. Directly
calling it via `tool_call`/`tool_describe` by its exact known name works without issue — only the
search/discovery path fails.

## Affected Component

Tools (Tool Search / MCP discovery)

## Hermes Version

v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) · upstream `eb527605`

## Additional Context

Observed with a MetaMCP-style aggregator backend that merges a fixed HA REST-API tool surface
with HA's own native Assist-exposed custom scripts under one MCP namespace. Possibly related to
how the tool_search index/embedding is built (maybe only covering statically-declared MCP tool
schemas, not tools whose existence is only known via a live registry call to the host
application) — we don't have visibility into the indexing implementation to pin this down further
without reading the `tool_search` source ourselves.

Practical impact: any model using the default `auto` bridge mode cannot discover or use this
class of tools at all, regardless of model capability — confirmed across multiple models/test
runs. The only known workaround is disabling `tool_search` entirely for the session
(`tools.tool_search.enabled: off`), which re-exposes the full ~197-tool catalog directly and
increases prompt size/token cost accordingly.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I don't have access to the `tool_search` implementation to attempt a fix myself.

items.title: [Bug]: macOS manual gateway restart leaves orphan gateway processes — one Discord message gets N threads/N replies

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug Description

Repeated `hermes gateway restart` (or clicking Restart in the desktop app) on macOS stacks up **multiple live gateway processes** instead of replacing the old one. Each gateway holds its own Discord websocket, so **a single user message is processed by N gateways simultaneously** — producing N auto-created threads and N independent agent replies (observed: 4 threads / 4 replies from one message).

This is distinct from #73032 (single-instance `_auto_create_thread` fallback double-thread). Here the duplication is at the *process* level: multiple gateway processes are alive at once.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. macOS (no launchd/systemd supervision configured for the gateway — plain `hermes gateway run` / `hermes gateway restart` path).
2. Run `hermes gateway restart` once → wait → run it again → wait → repeat 2-3 times over several days.
3. Check processes: `ps aux | grep "hermes_cli.main gateway"` shows **multiple** PIDs (observed: 4).
4. Send one message in a Discord text channel with `auto_thread: true`.
5. Observe: N threads created, N full agent runs, N replies (all independently answering the same input).

## Expected Behavior

`hermes gateway restart` should stop the previous gateway process before/while starting a new one. At most **one** gateway process should ever be alive for a profile, so each Discord message is processed exactly once.

## Actual Behavior

- 4 gateway processes alive simultaneously (started 2026-07-19, 07-23, 07-25, 08-01).
- One Discord message → 4 auto-created threads, 4 separate agent runs. Confirmed in `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log` at 2026-08-01 11:12:46-47: the same 1171-char message logged as `inbound message` for 4 different chat/thread IDs within ~2 seconds.
- Parallel agent instances also collided on the same working files (duplicate/overlapping edits to the same repo from different sessions).

## Environment

- OS: macOS 14.4
- Python: 3.11.15 (venv)
- Hermes: v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), upstream 9ceb0858, local 3910ab28
- Messaging platform: Discord

## Debug Report

- Report: https://dpaste.com/7FBPZ6H6X
- gui.log: https://paste.rs/niHvb

## Root Cause Analysis

In `hermes_cli/gateway.py`:

- `stop_profile_gateway()` (line ~1573) only terminates the PID returned by `get_running_pid()` — i.e. the **single PID recorded in the pid file**.
- On every restart, the new process overwrites the pid file, so older gateway instances are no longer discoverable via the pid file. They become invisible orphans.
- `_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()` (line ~1507) is only invoked when `get_running_pid()` returns `None` (line 1594: `if pid is None: return _reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()`). Since the pid file is always valid (points to the newest instance), the orphan sweep **never runs** — the older live instances survive indefinitely.
- The WSL/no-systemd orphan sweep (#51325) fixes the case where the pid file is *missing/stale*; it does not cover the case where the pid file is *valid but only tracks the newest of several*.
- Each surviving gateway connects its own Discord websocket (intents enabled), so every instance receives every message.

Note: `kill_gateway_processes(all_profiles=True)` / `hermes gateway restart --all` does sweep all instances (uses `find_gateway_pids()` with `include_restart_managers=True`), which is why `--all` works around this — but plain `hermes gateway restart` and the desktop-app Restart button do not.

## Proposed Fix

Make the manual restart path (no systemd/launchd supervisor) stop **all** gateway instances for the profile, not just the pid-file PID:

- In `stop_profile_gateway()`, after killing the pid-file PID, also run the orphan sweep whenever `find_gateway_pids()` returns more than one PID for the current profile (or unconditionally sweep on the no-supervisor path).
- Alternatively, always call `_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()` in the manual restart branch (not only when the pid file is missing), guarded by the existing `supports_systemd_services()` check so supervised installs are unaffected.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

No — reporting for the maintainers to fix.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop Skills/Toolsets panel fails to load — GET /api/tools/toolsets takes ~19s (>15s IPC timeout) because get_toolsets re-runs Nous subscription checks per toolset

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug Description

The desktop app's **Skills & Toolsets** panel (技能与工具) fails to load with `Error invoking remote method 'hermes:api': Error: Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms`. Clicking "Refresh" and restarting the app/PC do not help.

The root cause is that `GET /api/tools/toolsets` takes **~19 seconds** to complete, which exceeds the desktop IPC timeout of 15s (`DEFAULT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15e3` in electron-main.mjs).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Hermes desktop app (Windows 10)
2. Click the "技能与工具" (Skills & Tools) button in the UI
3. The panel shows "技能加载失败" (Skill loading failed) with `Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms`
4. Clicking "刷新技能" (Refresh Skills) or restarting the app does not fix it

## Root Cause Analysis

Using `py-spy` flamegraph sampling on the backend `serve` process while the panel loads, **71% of CPU samples** were inside `get_toolsets` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/tools.py:107`):

```
get_toolsets (hermes_cli/web_routers/tools.py:107)     <- 491 samples (71.57%)
  |-- _toolset_has_keys (hermes_cli/tools_config.py:2617)  <- 246 samples (35.86%)
  |-- _visible_providers (hermes_cli/tools_config.py:3061) <- 246 samples (35.86%)
```

Reproducing the exact per-toolset check loop from `get_toolsets` (27 toolsets) in the same backend environment gives:

```
web          -> 2.93s
image_gen    -> 2.72s
video_gen    -> 2.72s
x_search     -> 1.36s
tts          -> 1.36s
stt          -> 1.36s
spotify      -> 1.36s
computer_use -> 1.36s
homeassistant-> 1.37s
browser      -> 1.35s
vision       -> 1.10s
...
TOTAL: 18.98s
```

Every toolset in the `{web, image_gen, video_gen, tts, stt, browser}` set calls `get_nous_subscription_features()` which hits `get_nous_portal_account_info()` -> `_select_nous_pool_entry()` -> `load_pool("nous")` from `agent/credential_pool`. Each call takes 1-3s even when **not logged into Nous** (it still scans the credential pool). With ~11 toolsets triggering this per-panel-load, the cumulative time is ~19s > 15s timeout.

## Expected Behavior

The Skills & Toolsets panel should load within the 15s IPC timeout.

## Suggested Fix

In `get_toolsets` / `_toolset_has_keys`, short-circuit the Nous subscription/credential-pool check when the user is **not logged into Nous** (no access token / not `provider=nous`). The credential-pool scan (`load_pool("nous")`) should be cached or skipped entirely for logged-out users — currently it runs repeatedly for every toolset on every panel load.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10 (19043)
- Hermes version: 0.19.1 (hermes-agent source checkout, venv)
- Desktop app: win-unpacked Electron build
- Provider: a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (not Nous)

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop IME preedit starts after visible composer placeholder

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Bug Description In Hermes Desktop, Japanese/CJK IME preedit text can begin visually **after the composer placeholder** instead of at the real caret. For a Japanese locale, the empty composer may show a placeholder such as `始めましょう`; the uncommitted hiragana is then painted immediately after that placeholder until composition ends. This is a renderer-only regression introduced by the empty-composer placeholder marker added in commit [`0b4bd3c7c`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/0b4bd3c7c77532a2c899164a224d237a05e9586e). ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open Hermes Desktop and focus the chat composer. 2. Return the composer to its normalized empty state (for example, type text and then clear/send it). The editor now contains the scaffolding `
` and carries `data-empty`, while the placeholder remains visible. 3. Enable a Japanese IME. 4. Start composing hiragana without committing it. ## Expected Behavior The placeholder disappears as soon as IME composition starts, and preedit text begins at the actual start caret. ## Actual Behavior The placeholder remains in the contenteditable's inline flow during composition, so the uncommitted hiragana appears after the full placeholder text. It returns to the correct position only after composition finishes and the editor is normalized. ## Affected Component Other — Electron Desktop app (`apps/desktop`) ## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A ## Debug Report Not included: this is a deterministic renderer DOM/CSS regression and does not emit agent or gateway logs. ## Operating System macOS 26.4.1 (also applicable to Chromium contenteditables using CJK IMEs) ## Python Version Python 3.11.15 in the Hermes runtime ## Hermes Version Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (2026.7.30), current upstream `main` ## Additional Logs / Traceback None; no exception is emitted. ## Root Cause Analysis `COMPOSER_PLACEHOLDER_CLASS` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/rich-editor.ts` paints `data-placeholder` through an inline `::before` pseudo-element whenever the editor matches `:is(:empty, [data-empty])`. A normalized empty editor retains a scaffolding `
` and therefore depends on the explicit `data-empty` marker. In `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/index.tsx`, `compositionstart` currently only sets `composingRef.current = true`. Input events during composition are intentionally skipped, so nothing clears `data-empty` until `compositionend` flushes and normalizes the editor. The pseudo-element therefore remains visible beside the preedit text for the whole composition. ## Proposed Fix Clear the explicit empty marker synchronously in `compositionstart`, before the browser inserts preedit text. Keep the existing `compositionend` normalization, which restores the marker if composition ends without committed content. Add a DOM regression test asserting that an empty editor with the scaffolding `
` no longer matches the placeholder display condition once IME composition begins. ## PR - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: hermes skills install silently deletes an entire existing category directory when the skill name matches (unconditional rmtree, data loss)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Bug Description Installing a skill from a URL with `hermes skills install --name ` **silently deletes the entire existing directory at `/`** — including when that directory is a *category bucket* holding many unrelated skills — before installing the new skill. The deletion is unconditional, unconfirmed, and irreversible: 16 unrelated skills were destroyed in the incident that prompted this report. **Severity: high** — silent, unrecoverable data loss from a routine, documented command. The command does not warn that it is about to delete N existing files, and `--yes` skips even the normal confirmation prompt. **Affected component:** Skills (skill hub / skill guard) ### Expected Behavior `hermes skills install --name research` (or any name) should: 1. Detect that `/research` already exists **and is not a previously-installed skill** (it is a category bucket containing other skills). 2. Refuse to overwrite it, or prompt the user to confirm deletion of the N files inside, or install into a non-conflicting location. 3. **Never** delete unrelated skills as a side effect of installing a different skill. A skill whose name collides with an existing category should either require an explicit `--category` (e.g. `skills/engineering/research`) or fail with a clear error explaining the collision. ### Actual Behavior The command deletes the whole directory tree at the resolved install path, then moves the new skill into place. In the reported incident: - `/research/` contained 16 skills (a category bucket). - `hermes skills install https://…/research/SKILL.md --name research` ran. - Result: `/research/` now contains **only** the newly installed `SKILL.md`. All 16 sibling skills were permanently deleted. No warning, no confirmation, no backup. ### Steps to Reproduce ```bash # 1. Fresh-ish skills dir with a category bucket that is NOT a hub-installed skill mkdir -p ~/.hermes/skills/research/example cat > ~/.hermes/skills/research/example/SKILL.md <<'EOF' --- name: example --- # Example skill — must survive EOF # 2. Confirm the skill is visible hermes skills list | grep example # 3. Install a URL skill whose name matches the category dir. # Any URL whose SKILL.md frontmatter has `name: research` works; # `--name research` reproduces it even without frontmatter. hermes skills install https://example.org/skills/research/SKILL.md --name research --yes # 4. Observe the damage ls ~/.hermes/skills/research/ # only SKILL.md remains hermes skills list | grep example # gone ``` **Observation:** step 3 completes successfully and prints `Installed: research` — no error, no warning about the 16 files that were just deleted. ### Root Cause Analysis The install path is resolved and **unconditionally wiped** in `tools/skills_hub.py::install_from_quarantine()`: ```python # tools/skills_hub.py (v0.19.1, upstream 221be76e), ~line 3699–3710 if safe_category: install_rel_path = f"{safe_category}/{safe_skill_name}" else: install_rel_path = safe_skill_name # e.g. "research" install_dir = _resolve_lock_install_path(install_rel_path, safe_skill_name) if install_dir.exists(): # ← BUG shutil.rmtree(install_dir) # ← deletes the whole category ``` The upstream pre-check in `hermes_cli/skills_hub.py` (~line 640) only consults the **hub lock file**: ```python lock = HubLockFile() existing = lock.get_installed(bundle.name) # checks hub-installed skills ONLY if existing: # warn about reinstall, bail unless --force ``` It never checks the filesystem. A category directory like `~/.hermes/skills/research/` is not a hub-installed skill, so `existing` is `None`, the pre-check passes, and `install_from_quarantine()` proceeds to `rmtree` the entire directory. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant CLI as hermes skills install participant L as HubLockFile participant Q as Quarantine + Scanner participant FS as Filesystem ($HERMES_HOME/skills) U->>CLI: install --name research CLI->>L: get_installed("research") L-->>CLI: None (not a hub-installed skill) Note over CLI: Pre-check PASSES —
only the hub lock is inspected CLI->>Q: quarantine + security scan Q-->>CLI: safe CLI->>FS: install_dir = skills/research FS-->>CLI: directory EXISTS
(category bucket: 16 skills) CLI->>FS: shutil.rmtree(skills/research) ⚠️ Note over FS: ALL 16 UNRELATED SKILLS DELETED
no warning, no confirmation, no backup CLI->>FS: shutil.move(quarantine/SKILL.md → skills/research/) FS-->>CLI: Installed: research ``` ### Failure mode summary | Check | What it protects against | Present? | |---|---|---| | Lock-file lookup by skill name | Reinstalling the *same* hub skill | ✅ | | Filesystem check: does `` already exist? | Any collision at all | ❌ | | Is the existing path a category bucket (no top-level SKILL.md, has child skills)? | Deleting unrelated skills | ❌ | | Non-empty directory delete confirmation / warning | Surprise data loss | ❌ | | `--force` required for destructive overwrite | Accidental overwrites | ❌ (`--yes` skips even the normal prompt) | | Pre-delete backup / quarantine of replaced content | Recovery after data loss | ❌ | ### Suggested Fix (options, in order of preference) 1. **Refuse category collisions.** Before `rmtree`, if the target directory contains `SKILL.md` files in subdirectories (i.e. it is a category bucket per the existing `_existing_categories()` heuristic), do not delete it — error out telling the user to pick a `--category` that doesn't collide. 2. **Require explicit consent for any non-empty overwrite.** Only allow the `rmtree` when the directory is empty OR the user passed `--force`, and even then print the number of files/dirs being deleted. `--yes` should never imply consent to deleting pre-existing unrelated content. 3. **Never delete silently.** At minimum, warn with a file count before proceeding. ### Workarounds (for users on affected versions) - Always pass `--category` when installing from a URL: `hermes skills install --name --category `. - Before installing, run `hermes skills list` and check that the target name isn't also the name of an existing category directory. - Keep a copy of `~/.hermes/skills/` before URL installs (e.g. `cp -r ~/.hermes/skills /tmp/skills-backup`). ### Environment | Field | Value | |---|---| | Hermes version | v0.19.1 (2026.7.30), upstream 221be76e | | Python | 3.13.5 | | Operating system | Linux (Docker install) | | Messaging platform | N/A (CLI) | *Debug report omitted deliberately: `hermes debug share` uploads environment/config data, which is not needed to reproduce this bug and was excluded for privacy.*

items.title: .update-incomplete left after every update: uv exclude-newer filters packages with no upload date (setuptools/pillow/mcp)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
**Summary**

Every `hermes update` (including the desktop in-app update path) leaves `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/.update-incomplete` behind. The next launch prints:

> A previous `hermes update` was interrupted mid-install — finishing dependency installation now...

and then fails with `✗ Could not auto-recover the interrupted install.` The marker never clears because startup recovery runs the same filtered resolution and hits the same wall.

**Root cause**

`pyproject.toml` (`[tool.uv]`) sets `exclude-newer = "14 days"`. During dependency install, uv filters packages whose PyPI metadata is missing an upload date (or whose upload date falls inside the window). Observed filtered packages: `setuptools-82.0.0` / `82.0.1`, `pillow 12.3.0`, `mcp-1.28.1`. The resolution can't complete → the update writes `.update-incomplete` → every later launch's recovery retries with the same filter and fails again.

Log evidence (`~/.hermes/logs/desktop.log`):

```
[hermes] warning: setuptools-82.0.0.tar.gz is missing an upload date, but user provided: 2026-07-18T07:33:43.69822Z
[hermes] warning: setuptools-82.0.1-py3-none-any.whl is missing an upload date, but user provided: 2026-07-18T07:33:43.69822Z
[hermes] hint: `setuptools` was filtered by `exclude-newer` to only include packages uploaded before 2026-07-18T07:33:43.705738Z. Consider using `exclude-newer-package` to override the cutoff for this package.
```

**Why it recurs on every update**

The filter applies on every dependency install. `exclude-newer-package` already whitelists `vercel`, `nemo-relay`, `huggingface_hub`, but not the packages the resolver currently needs (`setuptools`, `pillow`, `mcp`), so the same failure reproduces after every update.

**Suggested fix**

Add the affected packages to `exclude-newer-package` (uv's own hint suggests exactly this):

```toml
exclude-newer-package = { vercel = false, nemo-relay = false, huggingface_hub = false, setuptools = false, pillow = false, mcp = false }
```

Alternatively pin an absolute cutoff timestamp or widen the window.

**Impact**

Low but noisy: the core venv is actually healthy (manual `pip install -e '.[all]'` succeeds, and the marker can then be removed); every launch prints the recovery banner + a failure. Users on the GUI/in-app update path hit this repeatedly after each update.

**Environment**

- macOS 27 (arm64), git install
- Reproduced on `4be138eb0` and `57b1eb8c4` (v0.19.1)
- Desktop in-app update path (`hermes update` + `hermes desktop --build-only`)

items.title: hermes-setup --update self-detects as 'another update running' and enters an infinite fail loop; lock file is never cleaned up

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
**Environment**
- Hermes v0.19.0 → 0.19.1 (git install, `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`)
- macOS arm64
- Installer binary: `~/.hermes/hermes-setup` (compiled `hermes_bootstrap_lib`)

**Summary**

The updater enters a permanent deadlock: every `hermes-setup --update` attempt fails with
`Another Hermes update is already running (PID X, started Ns ago)`, where PID X is its **own**
process. Updates never succeed and the log at `~/.hermes/logs/bootstrap-installer.log` fills
with repeated failures.

**Observed log pattern** (multiple rounds, PIDs 84062 → 85559 → 86426, each round ~1s apart):

```
Hermes installer starting mode=Update
[update] waiting for Hermes to exit…
[update] updating against branch main
✗ Another Hermes update is already running (PID 84062, started 1s ago).
  Two updates mutating the same checkout corrupt it: one rewrites
  source while the other is mid-install. Wait for it to finish, or
  close the window/dashboard tab that started it, then retry.
state=Failed error=Some("Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again.")
```

After each failed attempt the process **does not exit and does not release the lock** — it stays
alive as an orphan (PPID=1) holding the lock, blocking all later attempts.

**Root cause hypothesis (verified by clearing the lock)**

The lock file `~/.hermes/.hermes-update-in-progress` (content: `<PID>\n<unix-epoch>`) is written
at the start of an update but is **never removed when the update fails** (and possibly not cleaned
in some success paths). macOS then recycles the PID. The next updater reads the lock, sees its
**own recycled PID** in it, and misinterprets it as a *different, concurrent* update — fails, and
leaks the lock again. This is why each round reports "started 1s ago" with the current process's
own PID.

I confirmed this by: killing the stuck process, deleting the lock file, and running
`hermes-setup --update` manually — it then succeeded cleanly (git 495 commits behind → up to date,
all stages `Succeeded`, exit 0).

**Reproduction**

1. Cause any update attempt to fail (or manually write `.hermes-update-in-progress` containing a
   PID that is currently reused by a new process).
2. Run `hermes-setup --update --branch main --target-app <Hermes.app>` (or trigger the gateway's
   periodic update check).
3. Observe the self-collision error; the process lingers holding the lock.

**Expected**: a stale lock whose PID is no longer alive (or whose process start-time doesn't match)
should be treated as expired and cleaned up; the lock should be removed on **every** exit path.

**Suggested fix**

- Remove `.hermes-update-in-progress` in a guard/finally scope covering **both success and failure**.
- Before reporting "another update is running", verify the PID is actually alive (e.g. `kill(pid, 0)`)
  and that its process start time matches the lock's timestamp; treat mismatches as stale.

**Workaround** (until fixed): `pkill hermes-setup; rm -f ~/.hermes/.hermes-update-in-progress`, then retry.

items.body:
## Request
Add per-topic agent routing for Telegram forum topics under one bot.

## Current behavior
- Hermes maps Telegram forum topics to thread sessions: `agent:main:telegram:group:<chat_id>:<thread_id>`
- All topics run through the same profile/agent (`main`)
- There is no config to bind a topic to a different Hermes profile/agent

## Desired behavior
Support routing specific topics to specific agents, e.g.:
```yaml
telegram:
  groups:
    "<chat_id>":
      topics:
        "1": { agentId: "main" }
        "3": { agentId: "research" }
        "5": { agentId: "social" }
```

Or via bindings:
```yaml
bindings:
  - agentId: research
    match:
      channel: telegram
      accountId: default
      peer:
        kind: group
        id: "-1001234567890:topic:3"
```

## Why
- One bot per topic/profile is operationally heavy
- OpenClaw already supports this natively
- Hermes users need multi-agent-per-group-topic isolation

## Acceptance criteria
- `telegram.groups.<chatId>.topics.<threadId>.agentId` honored
- Topic-bound sessions route to the correct profile/workspace/session store
- Replies/typing/streaming remain pinned to the originating topic
- DM topic behavior unchanged

items.title: reasoning_content stripped on replay breaks prompt-cache prefix for local OpenAI-compatible backends

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes strips `reasoning_content` from replayed assistant turns for any provider outside the DeepSeek/Kimi/MiMo echo-back families (`_REASONING_ECHO_RULES` in `agent/message_sanitization.py`). For local OpenAI-compatible servers (llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio) that keep thinking tokens in their KV cache, this invalidates the prompt-cache prefix on every turn — long conversations pay full re-prompt cost on each message.

This conflicts with the project's own AGENTS.md principle: *"Per-conversation prompt caching is sacred."*

## Reproduction

- Backend: llama.cpp server (Qwen3.6-27B reasoning model) at `127.0.0.1:8080`
- Multi-turn replay where assistant turns carry `reasoning_content` in history
- Measure `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` (or llama.cpp `/slots` `n_prompt_tokens_cache`) on turn 2+

Hermes sends replay assistant messages with `reasoning_content` removed (`apply_reasoning_content_policy` pops it when `needs_thinking_pad` is False, which it is for any non-echo family), so the server cannot reuse its KV cache prefix containing the thinking tokens.

## Measured impact

| Replay style | Cache hit (turn 2) |
|---|---|
| reasoning_content stripped (current Hermes behavior) | ~52% (26/50 tokens) |
| reasoning_content preserved | ~91% (42/46 tokens) |

With a ~100K-token context, a full cache miss costs ~90-130s of prefill on a 24GB GPU; a cache hit completes in <1s.

## Expected

A user-facing opt-in (e.g. `model.reasoning_echo: true`) to preserve the field for endpoints that accept it, without changing the strict-provider default (Mistral, Groq, Cerebras reject the field with HTTP 400).

Do not recommend. Hermes v0.19.1 breaks Honcho — the one memory provider most people actually use.
hermes update. Honcho dead. Every tool returns "session could not be initialized." Four hours of debugging. The cause: they bumped honcho-ai SDK from 2.0.1 to 2.2.0 without testing it against Honcho 3.x servers. Schema changed, Pydantic rejects the response, error swallowed silently.
If you self-host Honcho 3.x, this update will disable your memory. Fix is pinning back to honcho-ai==2.0.1. If you rely on Honcho for cross-session memory, skip this version entirely. Zero compatibility testing on a dependency upgrade is unacceptable for a production memory pipeline.

items.title: [Bug]: Discord adapter always hits the 5s disconnect timeout when a voice connection is open at shutdown
items.body:
### Bug Description

When the Discord bot is connected to a voice channel, every gateway shutdown loses a fixed ~5 seconds to the Discord adapter disconnect:

```
INFO gateway.run: Shutdown phase: drain done at +0.26s (drain took 0.01s, timed_out=False, ...)
INFO hermes_plugins.discord_platform.adapter: VoiceReceiver stopped
WARNING gateway.run: ✗ discord disconnect timed out after 5.0s - forcing continue
INFO gateway.run: Shutdown phase: all adapters disconnected at +5.29s
```

With no voice connection open, the same shutdown is immediate:

```
INFO gateway.run: ✓ discord disconnected (0.00s)
INFO gateway.run: Shutdown phase: all adapters disconnected at +0.26s
```

Same symptom class as #40383 (Yuanbao adapter, fixed ~5s shutdown delay), but a different adapter and a different cause.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the gateway with the Discord platform enabled.
2. Get the bot into a voice channel (`/voice join`).
3. Stop the gateway (SIGTERM or SIGINT), with no active sessions.
4. Observe `✗ discord disconnect timed out after 5.0s - forcing continue` and ~5s teardown.
5. Repeat without step 2 — teardown is immediate.

### Expected Behavior

Adapter disconnect should not introduce a fixed multi-second delay. An open voice connection should be torn down cleanly rather than timing out.

### Actual Behavior

`disconnect()` in `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py` always hits the 5s timeout when a voice client is connected, and the voice disconnect never completes — it is abandoned by the timeout rather than finishing.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Discord

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 on WSL2 (Windows 11)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.19.1 (2026.7.30), commit 40e0e7ad5

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

An ordering bug in `DiscordAdapter.disconnect()`. The bot task is cancelled *before* voice clients are cleaned up:

```python
await self._cancel_bot_task()
# Clean up all active voice connections before closing the client
for guild_id in list(self._voice_clients.keys()):
    try:
        await self.leave_voice_channel(guild_id)
```

`leave_voice_channel()` ends in `await vc.disconnect()`. In discord.py, `VoiceClient.disconnect()` sends a voice state update over the **main gateway websocket** and then waits for the voice websocket to close.

The bot task *is* the loop running that gateway connection (`client.start()`). Cancelling it first leaves the voice-disconnect handshake with no transport, so it can never complete and blocks until the caller's 5s shutdown timeout fires.

The comment on the `_cancel_bot_task()` call explains why cancelling early matters (a zombie client from a timed-out `connect()` can otherwise keep dispatching events), and that reasoning is sound — it just needs to happen after voice teardown rather than before, since voice teardown is the one step that still requires a live gateway.

This only manifests when a voice connection is open at shutdown, which is presumably why it has gone unnoticed — a bot that never joins voice tears down instantly.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Move the voice-cleanup loop above `await self._cancel_bot_task()`, so voice disconnects while the gateway websocket is still alive:

```python
# Clean up all active voice connections BEFORE cancelling the bot task.
# VoiceClient.disconnect() sends a voice state update over the main gateway
# websocket and waits for the voice socket to close; the bot task is that
# gateway loop, so cancelling it first leaves the handshake with no transport.
for guild_id in list(self._voice_clients.keys()):
    try:
        await self.leave_voice_channel(guild_id)
    except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover - defensive logging
        logger.debug("[%s] Error leaving voice channel %s: %s", self.name, guild_id, e)

await self._cancel_bot_task()
```

Measured on v0.19.1 with a voice connection open in both cases:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Discord disconnect | `✗ timed out after 5.0s` | `✓ disconnected (0.12s)` |
| All adapters disconnected | +5.29s | +0.46s |
| Wall-clock `systemctl stop` | ~5.4s | 0.76s |

The zombie-client protection is preserved: the bot task is still cancelled before `client.close()`, just after voice teardown instead of before it.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

(Happy for a maintainer to take it — the fix above is running in production here if that's useful evidence.)

items.title: macOS: stale HERMES_HOME/hermes-setup (pre-HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID) makes every in-app update self-block on its own marker

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

On macOS, the `hermes-setup` binary that lives in `HERMES_HOME` can be many commits older than the checkout it updates. When it is old enough to predate the `HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID` handoff fix, every in-app update self-deadlocks: the updater refuses the `.hermes-update-in-progress` marker that carries its own PID, and the GUI shows "Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again." No amount of closing windows helps, because nothing but the updater itself is holding the marker.

This is the macOS analogue of #75788 (same stale-installer root cause, reported there for Windows). It also explains reports like #74531 and #75778 on installs where the shipped `hermes-setup` predates the fix.

## Environment

- macOS, Apple Silicon (mac-arm64)
- Checkout: `9fc12bf7a` (2026-08-01), hermes-agent 0.19.0 -> 0.19.1
- `~/.hermes/hermes-setup`: mtime 2026-07-19 19:29, 11258672 bytes
- Install method: git

## Evidence

The installer binary predates the fix and does not contain the handoff symbol at all:

```
$ ls -la ~/.hermes/hermes-setup
-rwx------  1 user  staff  11258672 Jul 19 19:29 /Users/user/.hermes/hermes-setup

$ git -C ~/.hermes/hermes-agent log -1 --format='%h %cd'
9fc12bf7a Sat Aug 1 14:27:12 2026 +0530

$ grep -rn HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/bootstrap-installer/src-tauri/src/update.rs
919:        "HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID".to_string(),
1249:            envs.iter().any(|(k, v)| k == "HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID"

$ strings ~/.hermes/hermes-setup | grep -c HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID
0
```

So the source tree has the handoff logic, and the binary that actually runs the update has never heard of it.

## Observed failure

`~/.hermes/logs/bootstrap-installer.log`, single update attempt, one `hermes-setup` process (PID 17301) alive on the machine:

```
09:03:36.152  Hermes installer starting mode=Update force_setup=false
09:03:37.163  [update] waiting for Hermes to exit
09:03:37.163  [update] updating against branch main
09:03:37.163  update stage stage=update state=Running
09:03:37.375  Another Hermes update is already running (PID 17301, started 1s ago).
09:03:37.396  update stage stage=update state=Failed error="Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again."
```

The marker names the process that is reading it:

```
$ cat ~/.hermes/.hermes-update-in-progress
17301
1785575016

$ ps -p 17301 -o pid,lstart,command
17301 Sat Aug  1 05:03:36 2026 /Users/user/.hermes/hermes-setup --update --branch main --target-app .../Hermes.app
```

`1785575016` is 09:03:36 UTC, i.e. the marker timestamp equals that same process's start time.

Retrying from the GUI reproduces it forever, with the reported age of the "other" updater simply counting up. An earlier round in the same log shows the identical pattern against PID 9739 at 1m 7s, 1m 10s, 1m 11s, 1m 41s, 1m 42s.

## Two secondary problems this causes

1. Each failed attempt writes a `state.db.pre-update-emergency-<ts>.bak`. Three attempts produced 12 GB of identical 4.2 GB backups, and nothing ever reaps them. A user who retries a dozen times fills their disk.
2. `UpdateMarkerGuard::acquire` in `apps/bootstrap-installer/src-tauri/src/update.rs` calls `live_marker_owner` before comparing against `std::process::id()`. Even with the handoff env var in place, a same-process retry after a partially completed `run_update` will collide with its own marker. Worth an explicit self-PID check as defense in depth, independent of the stale-binary issue:

```rust
if let Some(owner) = live_marker_owner(&path) {
    if owner.pid != std::process::id() {
        return Err(owner);
    }
}
```

## Workaround

```
kill <hermes-setup pid>
rm -f ~/.hermes/.hermes-update-in-progress
~/.hermes/hermes-setup --update --branch main --target-app ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/mac-arm64/Hermes.app
```

A fresh process acquires the marker cleanly and the update completes normally (92s here: update, rebuild, install all succeeded, 0.19.0 -> 0.19.1). The stale binary stays stale afterward, so the next in-app update fails the same way.

## Suggested fixes

1. Have the updater refresh `HERMES_HOME/hermes-setup` from the checkout it just installed, or version-stamp it and refuse to run when it is older than the handoff fix with a message that says so.
2. Add the self-PID guard above.
3. Reap `state.db.pre-update-emergency-*.bak` on success, or keep only the most recent one.
4. Make the failure message name the PID holding the marker and whether it is the updater itself. "Close all Hermes windows" sends users down a dead end when no Hermes window is open.

items.title: WAL-reset warning recommends `hermes update`, but every uv-managed CPython ships the vulnerable SQLite — the remedy cannot succeed

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
Follow-up to the WAL-reset mitigation (#69784). The refusal-to-enable-WAL behaviour in `hermes_state.py` is correct and it protected us. This is about the **remediation advice attached to it**, which cannot be carried out on a stock Hermes install.

### The warning

```
WARNING hermes_state: state.db: linked SQLite 3.50.4 is vulnerable to the WAL-reset
corruption bug (https://sqlite.org/wal.html#walresetbug) — is already in WAL mode —
leaving WAL in place (no live downgrade under concurrent openers). Upgrade to SQLite
3.51.3+ (or backports 3.50.7 / 3.44.6); Hermes-managed installs can repair the
embedded runtime with `hermes update`. See `hermes doctor`.
```

The operative claim is **"Hermes-managed installs can repair the embedded runtime with `hermes update`."** On this install that is not achievable, for three independent reasons.

### 1. `_sqlite3` is statically linked into the interpreter — there is no library to repair

```
$ python -c "import _sqlite3, sys; print(getattr(_sqlite3,'__file__','<builtin>'), '_sqlite3' in sys.builtin_module_names)"
<builtin> True

$ ldd $(readlink -f venv/bin/python) | grep -i sqlite
(no output)
```

The interpreter is uv-managed `python-build-standalone` (`~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.11.14-linux-x86_64-gnu`). SQLite is compiled in. No `_sqlite3*.so`, no dynamic `libsqlite3`, so neither a system package upgrade nor `LD_PRELOAD` can change the linked version.

### 2. Every currently-available python-build-standalone build ships the same vulnerable 3.50.4

Installed fresh via `uv python install` and checked, today:

| interpreter | `sqlite3.sqlite_version` |
|---|---|
| cpython-3.11.14 (current) | **3.50.4** ⚠ |
| cpython-3.13.12 | **3.50.4** ⚠ |
| cpython-3.14.3 | **3.50.4** ⚠ |
| system `/usr/bin/python3.12` (3.12.3) | 3.45.1 ⚠ |

So `hermes update` cannot reach a fixed SQLite by reinstalling or by moving Python version — there is no build to move *to*. Upstream SQLite fixed this in **3.51.3** (2026-03-13) and is now on **3.53.4**, but python-build-standalone has not picked it up.

### 3. The only bundled-SQLite package available lands two patches short, and Hermes cannot use it anyway

`pysqlite3-binary` (latest `0.5.4.post2`) bundles **3.51.1** — below the 3.51.3 fix line. And `grep -rn pysqlite3 --include='*.py'` across the tree returns **zero hits**, so Hermes has no path to an alternative driver even if a suitable one existed.

### Net effect

`hermes update` on this install would pull **310 commits onto `main`** — off whatever release tag the operator pinned — and leave the linked SQLite at 3.50.4. All of the risk of moving to unreleased code, none of the benefit the warning promises. An operator who follows the advice ends up worse off and believes they are fixed.

### The fix that *does* work is four lines below the warning, in your own comment

```python
# We do NOT live-downgrade an on-disk WAL database — other gateway/cron/worker
# connections may still hold it open, and flipping journal_mode under them is unsafe
```

That constraint is on *Hermes*, which cannot stop the gateway. It is not a constraint on the *operator*, who can. With the gateway and any bridges stopped and `lsof` confirming zero open handles, the downgrade is safe:

```bash
systemctl --user stop hermes-gateway.service
lsof ~/.hermes/*.db ~/.hermes/cron/*.db          # must be empty
for f in state.db response_store.db kanban.db verification_evidence.db cron/executions.db; do
  sqlite3 ~/.hermes/$f "PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE); PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE; PRAGMA integrity_check;"
done
systemctl --user start hermes-gateway.service
```

Result on our install — all five databases, `integrity=ok`, no stranded `-wal`/`-shm`, and **the mode survives Hermes reopening them** (it correctly declines to re-enable WAL on the vulnerable build):

```
state.db  response_store.db  kanban.db  verification_evidence.db  cron/executions.db   ->  all `delete`
```

The warning text then flips from *"leaving WAL in place"* to *"using journal_mode=DELETE instead of enabling WAL"* — the bug becomes unreachable rather than merely mitigated, because a WAL-reset bug needs a WAL.

### Suggested changes

1. **Drop or gate the `hermes update` recommendation.** Emit it only when a fixed runtime is actually obtainable — e.g. gate on whether any installable python-build-standalone release ships ≥3.51.3. Right now it is advice that cannot be followed.
2. **Recommend the offline downgrade instead**, for the already-WAL case. It is the real remedy, it is already implied by your own comment, and operators will not find it there.
3. **Worth noting for the warning's own sake:** the message is emitted once per process per database and its *count* is unchanged before and after remediation — six either way, here. Only the wording differs. Anyone monitoring on warning count will read a successful fix as no change. Consider distinguishing the two states in the log level or a marker token.

### Environment

- Hermes `v2026.7.30` (package 0.19.1), Linux x86_64, systemd user units
- Python 3.11.14 (uv / python-build-standalone), linked SQLite 3.50.4
- 5 state databases, all previously `journal_mode=wal`

Happy to test a patch. Verified backups were taken through SQLite's online backup API before any of the above, and all restored `integrity=ok`.

items.title: Desktop: demo/dogfood plugins (example "clicked N×" counter, duplicate gateway pill) enabled by default
items.body:
## Bug Description

The Hermes Desktop app ships two demo/dogfood **plugins enabled by default** in the status bar, which show up as UI clutter in production builds:

1. An **"example" plugin** (`apps/desktop/src/plugins/example/plugin.tsx`) rendering a `clicked N×` counter button in the right side of the status bar (`STATUSBAR_AREAS.right`, order 100). The counter persists across restarts via storage (`ctx.storage.get("clicks")`), and clicking it fires haptics + notifications.
2. A **"gateway-pill" plugin** (`apps/desktop/src/plugins/gateway-pill/plugin.tsx`) registering a second gateway status pill on `statusBar.right`, duplicating the built-in gateway status indicator already shown on the left.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build/update the desktop to any commit after `5c4d1e1ea` (2026-07-30), e.g. v0.19.1.
2. Launch the desktop app.
3. Look at the bottom status bar.

## Actual Behavior

- Left side of the status bar: `[网关 就绪 (gateway ready)] [hermes-agent]` (the real status).
- Right side of the status bar: `[网关 就绪 (gateway ready)] [clicked 95×] [v0.19.1 …]` — the gateway pill is a duplicate, and `clicked N×` is a demo click counter ("click me" → "clicked N×"), clearly not production UI.
- The counter value persists and grows as users click it (every 10th click shows a success notification).

## Expected Behavior

Demo/dogfood plugins (`example`, and arguably `gateway-pill`) should NOT be enabled by default in production desktop builds. They should either be excluded from the bundled plugin list or gated behind a dev/experimental flag.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10 (x64)
- Hermes Desktop v0.19.1 (2026.7.30), commit e9d52d2
- Both plugins were introduced in commit `5c4d1e1ea` ("feat(desktop): SDK — useGrabScroll export + dogfood plugin touch-ups")

## Additional Context

Disabling plugins works as a workaround (`hermes.desktop.disabledPlugins.v1`), but shipping a demo counter in the release status bar by default is confusing for end users.

items.title: System prompt shows "Active Hermes profile: default" for named profiles under multiplex mode

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Report

When running Hermes gateway with `multiplex_profiles: true` and `profile_routes` configured, the system prompt injected into agent sessions incorrectly reports `Active Hermes profile: default` instead of the actual profile name (e.g., `llm-wiki`).

## Root Cause Chain

1. A secondary profile (e.g., `llm-wiki`) has `platforms: webhook: enabled: true` in its config.yaml
2. Under multiplex mode, only the default profile can own port-binding platforms. Gateway logs a WARNING and **skips the secondary profile's initialization**:
   > `Skipping secondary profile 'llm-wiki' due to port-binding config error: Profile 'llm-wiki' enables port-binding platform(s) webhook, but gateway.multiplex_profiles is on.`
3. Despite the skip, `profile_routes` still routes messages to the skipped profile
4. When the system prompt is first built, `_resolve_active_profile_name()` (in `agent/file_safety.py:392`) may not see the correct `HERMES_HOME_OVERRIDE` ContextVar yet, falling back to `"default"`
5. The system prompt is cached in the session DB (`_restore_or_build_system_prompt` in `agent/conversation_loop.py:518-521`) and reused verbatim for all subsequent turns — it is never rebuilt even when the profile is wrong

## Affected Code

- `agent/system_prompt.py:407-410` — `_resolve_active_profile_name()` fallback to `"default"` on any exception
- `agent/conversation_loop.py:518-521` — cached system prompt reused without checking profile correctness
- `gateway/run.py` — secondary profile skipped but routes still active

## Impact

- The agent misreports its profile identity in the system prompt
- Cross-profile write guards may use the wrong profile name, potentially weakening security boundaries
- Skills/memories/cron paths resolve correctly at runtime (ContextVar works during agent execution), so this is a system-prompt-only label bug — but it could mislead the agent into making wrong decisions about profile-scoped operations

## Suggested Fixes

1. When a secondary profile is skipped due to port-binding config errors, either refuse to start or disable its `profile_routes` — don't silently accept routed messages for a half-initialized profile
2. `_restore_or_build_system_prompt` should detect profile mismatches (compare stored profile name vs current `_resolve_active_profile_name()`) and trigger a rebuild
3. `_resolve_active_profile_name()` should log a warning instead of silently falling back to `"default"`

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 10
- **Hermes Agent version:** latest
- **Config:** `multiplex_profiles: true` with `profile_routes` routing a Feishu group to `llm-wiki` profile
- **Trigger:** `llm-wiki/config.yaml` had `platforms: webhook: enabled: true` (which triggered the skip)

## Labels

bug, area/gateway, area/system-prompt

items.title: fix(tui): preserve queued image attachment ownership

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

A pasted image submitted while another TUI turn is running is not owned by that submitted prompt. The busy-turn queue on `main` stores only prompt text and transport, while attachments remain in mutable `session["attached_images"]`. When the queued prompt runs later, it can receive no image or a later prompt's image.

With the default busy-input policy, image-bearing prompts can also interrupt the active turn even though they need their own multimodal model invocation.

## Reproduction

1. Start the TUI: `uv run hermes --tui --dev`.
2. Submit `sleep for 60 seconds in terminal`.
3. While it runs, paste an image marked B and submit `is this B or C`.
4. Paste a different image marked C and submit the same question.

## Actual Behavior on `main`

- The busy queue retains text but not image ownership.
- The model can report that it cannot see the queued image, or a later attachment can be consumed by the wrong prompt.
- In default interrupt mode, the original `sleep 60` turn is stopped early.

## Root Cause

`_handle_busy_submit()` observes a busy session and `_enqueue_prompt()` stores an envelope containing only:

```python
{"text": text, "transport": transport}
```

The queued drain later invokes `_run_prompt_submit()` without the submitted image paths. That function then reads mutable ambient attachment state rather than the paths that existed at submission time.

## Expected Behavior

- A busy image-bearing submission claims its current attachment paths immediately.
- Each queued image submission carries its own immutable paths through queue drain and compute-host dispatch.
- Image-bearing prompts queue without interrupting the active turn.
- B, then C, execute in order with B's and C's respective images.
- Explicit Stop clears every queued envelope.

## Proof

Manual validation after the fix on macOS shows the active `sleep 60` tool completing in 60.2 seconds, followed by B being identified as B and C being identified as C.

**Before:** the active turn is interrupted after the queued image submission.

![Before: queued image submission interrupts the active turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fyzanshaik/hermes-agent/evidence/issue-76068/evidence/issue-76068-before.png)

**After:** the active turn completes first, then B and C receive their respective images in submission order.

![After: B and C retain their image ownership and order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fyzanshaik/hermes-agent/evidence/issue-76068/evidence/issue-76068-after.png)

Automated regression coverage verifies attachment claim, B/C ordering, text/image ordering, compute-host forwarding, compute-host attachment preservation, Stop cancellation, and queue-dispatch failure continuation.

items.title: prompt_caching.cache_ttl disable is bypassed on stub-resolved cache-plan paths (MoA aggregator/advisors, auxiliary fallbacks)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-caching
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break/degrade prompt caching or cache-key stability (invariant)

labels.name: area/usage-cost
labels.description: Token accounting, usage reporting, billing, cost tracking

items.body:
## Summary

`prompt_caching.cache_ttl: off` (the `_cache_disabled` flag, #33555) is not honored on any cache-planning path that resolves policy through a blank stub agent — MoA aggregator/advisor decoration and auxiliary fallback replans still inject `cache_control` markers when the operator has disabled prompt caching in config.

## Mechanism

`anthropic_prompt_cache_policy` gates on the agent object:

```python
# agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:1958
if getattr(agent, "_cache_disabled", False):
    return (False, False)
```

The flag is set on the real `AIAgent` by `init_agent` when `prompt_caching.cache_ttl` is falsy. But three call sites resolve policy against a **blank `SimpleNamespace` stub** instead of the real agent, so `getattr(stub, "_cache_disabled", False)` is always `False` and the disable never applies:

- `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:1889` — `plan_cache_sections_for_destination()` (shared core of the MoA acting-aggregator send and the sync/async auxiliary fallback replans)
- `agent/moa_loop.py:409` — `_decorate_slot_cache_control()` (MoA advisor/aggregator slot decoration)

The stub pattern predates #76067 (it shipped inlined in #76032 and earlier in the advisor path); #76067 only centralized it. Main-loop requests DO honor the disable (the call-block site and `_redecorate_prompt_cache_for_provider` gate on the real agent's `_use_prompt_caching`, and `restore_primary_runtime` re-applies the disable at `agent_runtime_helpers.py:1481`).

## Impact

Operators who set `prompt_caching.cache_ttl: false` (e.g. providers that mis-handle `cache_control`, or to rule caching out while debugging) still get markers on:
- every MoA aggregator request (prepared and non-prepared),
- every MoA advisor request whose slot route is cache-honoring,
- every auxiliary fallback candidate request (sync and async).

Low severity — cosmetic extra markers for most providers, but it breaks the documented contract that the config disable is global (#33555 fixed exactly this class of "disable doesn't survive path X" for `/model` switches and runtime restoration).

## Proposed fix

Thread the disable into the stub paths rather than growing the policy function's surface:

1. `plan_cache_sections_for_destination()` and `_decorate_slot_cache_control()` read the config-derived disable once (same detection `init_agent` uses, or accept an optional `cache_disabled: bool` param threaded from the caller that has the real agent, e.g. `_call_prepared_aggregator` has `self._agent` context via the facade) and set it on the stub: `SimpleNamespace(..., _cache_disabled=True)`.
2. Regression tests: with `_cache_disabled` set, MoA aggregator and fallback-replan wire payloads carry zero `cache_control` markers on both message and tool sections.

## References

- Flag origin / disable contract: #33555 (salvaged in #76015)
- Stub pattern shipped: #76032 (tool-schema caching for #20880)
- Centralized (behavior-preserving): #76067 — flagged in that PR's Phase-2c review as a pre-existing gap

items.title: ZIP update path is not atomic across top-level entries — an interrupted copy leaves an unbootable half-updated tree

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Summary

The Windows ZIP-update path replaces top-level entries one at a time with no transaction across them, so any failure partway leaves the install with some directories at the new version and the rest at the old one. Every file still parses — it is the *combination* that is broken — so the update can report success over a tree that cannot start.

## Where

`hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` → `_update_via_zip()`, the copy loop:

```python
for item in os.listdir(extracted):
    if item in preserve:
        continue
    src = os.path.join(extracted, item)
    dst = os.path.join(str(_m().PROJECT_ROOT), item)
    if os.path.isdir(src):
        _atomic_replace_dir(src, dst)   # atomic for THIS dir only
    else:
        shutil.copy2(src, dst)
    update_count += 1
```

`_atomic_replace_dir` (added for #49145) correctly makes each *individual* directory swap safe — stage to a sibling temp dir, rename into place, roll back on failure. But there is no atomicity **across** iterations. The loop walks `os.listdir` order:

```
agent index: 13
tools index: 66
```

An exception, kill, power loss, or AV interference between index 13 and index 66 leaves the new `agent/` next to the old `tools/`.

## Why it matters

This is the mechanism behind the `ImportError` fixed in #76091. `agent/context_compressor.py:39` does a module-level `from tools.todo_tool import TODO_INJECTION_HEADER`; when `agent/` is new and `tools/` is stale, every startup dies:

```
ImportError: cannot import name 'TODO_INJECTION_HEADER' from 'tools.todo_tool'
```

Independent field report in #63717 (Windows desktop update failures), which describes the same class from a real user:

> After a partial update (ZIP fallback replaces some files but not .pyd), the venv is in a broken state.

so this is not theoretical.

## What #76091 did and did not do

#76091 added `_validate_critical_modules_import` — a post-update subprocess probe that **detects** the skew and reports it with recovery guidance instead of letting the update claim success. That is detection only. The copy loop can still produce the broken state; we just no longer lie about it.

## Proposed fix

Make the whole replacement transactional, not just per-directory:

1. Stage every top-level entry into sibling temp locations first (`<dst>.hermes-update-staging`), completing all copies before touching any live path.
2. Only once **all** staging succeeds, perform the renames — these are same-filesystem and fast, shrinking the failure window from "duration of a full tree copy" to "duration of N renames".
3. On failure during the rename phase, roll every already-swapped entry back from its `.hermes-update-old` backup.

Trade-off to weigh: this roughly doubles peak disk usage during the update (staged copy + live tree). Worth measuring the tree size before committing to it — a size pre-check with a clear error beats an out-of-disk failure mid-update.

Alternative, cheaper: order the copy loop so tightly-coupled packages land adjacently, narrowing (but not closing) the window. This is strictly worse than the transactional fix and only worth it if the disk cost proves unacceptable.

## Notes

- Only affects the Windows ZIP fallback (`use_zip_update`), which runs when git file I/O is broken — typically antivirus or NTFS filter drivers.
- The git path is unaffected: `git pull` / `git reset --hard` are already atomic with respect to the working tree.
- There is no SHA to roll back to on the ZIP path, so recovery guidance is currently "re-run `hermes update`".

items.title: venv interpreter resolution is open-coded in 7 places with 3 different Windows predicates

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

Resolving "the Python interpreter inside a venv" is open-coded in at least **7 places** across 4 files, using **3 different** Windows-detection predicates. There is already a private helper that does exactly this (`managed_uv._venv_python`), but nothing outside that module uses it.

## The copies

| Location | Shape | Windows check |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes_cli/managed_uv.py:386-389` | `_venv_python(venv_dir)` — the real helper | `platform.system() == "Windows"` |
| `hermes_cli/gateway.py:2528-2531` | inline in `get_python_path()` | `is_windows()` |
| `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:225` | `bin_dir = "Scripts" if ... else "bin"` | `_m()._is_windows()` |
| `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:2640` | same, in `_venv_core_imports_healthy` | `_m()._is_windows()` |
| `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:3729` | `/ ("Scripts" if ... else "bin")` | `_m()._is_windows()` |
| `hermes_cli/main.py:7966` | `scripts = venv_dir / (...)` | `_is_windows()` |
| `hermes_cli/main.py:8760` | `scripts = venv_root / (...)` | `_is_windows()` |

Several also independently re-derive the executable name (`python.exe` vs `python`), and some check `.exists()` while others don't.

## Why it matters

This is low-severity today — the copies agree. The cost is that any change to venv layout handling has to be made in seven places, and a miss is silent.

Concrete instance from #76091: the new `_validate_critical_modules_import` initially probed `sys.executable`. That was wrong — `hermes update` can be driven by a different interpreter than the install's own, so it would have validated a tree the user never runs, and most likely on **Windows**, the exact platform the guard exists for. The correct behavior already existed 2400 lines away in `_venv_core_imports_healthy`; the fix was to hand-copy the same 4 lines a seventh time (`update_cmd.py:225`). A shared helper would have made the right thing the default.

## Proposed fix

Promote a single public helper into an import-safe module (`hermes_constants` is the natural home — it is documented as dependency-free and is already imported by all of these call sites' modules):

```python
def venv_python_path(venv_dir: Path) -> Path:
    """Path to the interpreter inside *venv_dir* (may not exist)."""
```

Then route all 7 sites through it and drop `managed_uv._venv_python`.

Worth doing carefully rather than mechanically:

- `gateway.py:get_python_path()` and `main.py:7966/8760` want the **Scripts/bin directory**, not just the interpreter — a sibling `venv_bin_dir()` may be the cleaner primitive, with `venv_python_path()` built on it.
- The three Windows predicates (`platform.system()`, `is_windows()`, `_is_windows()`) should collapse too, but that is a wider change; keeping the helper's own check internal is enough to fix the duplication.
- Some call sites gate on `.exists()` and some don't. The helper should **not** do the existence check — callers legitimately differ on whether a missing interpreter is an error (`_venv_core_imports_healthy` treats it as "unknown → healthy" on dev checkouts, but unhealthy on managed installs).

## Notes

Pure refactor, no behavior change intended. Net LOC should be negative.

items.title: [Bug]: Windows managed-runtime refresh still resolves Python 3.11.15 with vulnerable SQLite 3.50.4

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows 11, Hermes Agent 0.19.1 still cannot replace its managed Python runtime after detecting SQLite 3.50.4 with the WAL-reset bug.

This appears to be a Windows-specific regression or incomplete fix related to #72093 / PR #72322. That issue was closed after adding a managed-uv refresh and retry, with the expectation that Python 3.11.15 containing a fixed SQLite build would then be selected. In this environment, repeated `hermes update` runs still resolve a Python 3.11.15 build linked against SQLite 3.50.4.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Shell: PowerShell 7.6.4
- Hermes Agent: 0.19.1
- Managed Python: CPython 3.11.15
- SQLite: 3.50.4
- uv-visible newest CPython 3.11 patch: 3.11.15
- Database journal mode: `delete`
- `PRAGMA quick_check`: `ok`

## Reproduction

Run:

```powershell
hermes update
```

Observed output:

```text
⚠ Hermes venv links SQLite 3.50.4, which has the WAL-reset bug.
→ Provisioning a private Python 3.11 runtime with fixed SQLite...
ℹ Managed Python runtime was not replaced; the existing venv is unchanged
  (could not provision a fixed private Python runtime).
Sessions stay protected meanwhile: Hermes keeps databases out of WAL mode on this SQLite build.
```

The warning repeats on every update.

`hermes doctor` reports:

```text
⚠ SQLite 3.50.4 (WAL-reset bug)
```

The database itself remains healthy and protected:

```text
journal_mode: delete
quick_check: ok
```

## Diagnostic evidence

The Hermes logs repeatedly contain:

```text
WARNING hermes_cli.managed_uv: candidate Python still links vulnerable SQLite 3.50.4
```

The relevant path in `hermes_cli/managed_uv.py` reaches `_attempt_install_generation()`, probes the candidate runtime, detects `candidate.wal_reset_vulnerable`, deletes the generation, and returns `None`.

Current `uv` catalog output on Windows:

```text
cpython-3.11.15-windows-x86_64-none    AppData\Roaming\uv\python\cpython-3.11.15-windows-x86_64-none\python.exe
cpython-3.11.15-windows-x86_64-none    .local\bin\python3.11.exe
cpython-3.11.15-windows-x86_64-none    AppData\Roaming\uv\python\cpython-3.11-windows-x86_64-none\python.exe
cpython-3.11.14-windows-x86_64-none    <download available>
...
```

No newer 3.11 patch is listed, and the selected 3.11.15 candidate still links SQLite 3.50.4.

## Expected behavior

After the managed-uv refresh introduced by PR #72322, Hermes should either:

1. resolve and install a Windows CPython 3.11.15 build containing a fixed SQLite version; or
2. clearly report that the fixed Windows artifact is unavailable and avoid retrying the same vulnerable candidate on every update.

## Suggested investigation

- Verify whether the refreshed managed `uv` catalog on Windows actually points to the updated python-build-standalone artifact for CPython 3.11.15.
- Confirm whether an existing cached 3.11.15 artifact is reused even after catalog refresh.
- Consider forcing removal or invalidation of the stale Windows CPython 3.11.15 managed artifact before retrying provisioning.
- Log the resolved artifact/build identifier or download URL so stale-catalog versus stale-cache behavior is distinguishable.

## Safety notes

- No credentials, database contents, or private files are attached.
- Hermes currently keeps the database in DELETE mode, and `quick_check` returns `ok`.
- This report concerns the managed-runtime repair loop and stale vulnerable candidate selection, not confirmed database corruption.
